-This page documents a [[id:699A8D45-B67E-4D3E-9206-24FA17C51ADA][story]] in [[id:3CEE598D-47C8-4EC0-9E01-19CE79CCA4CD][Sprint 28]]. It captures the goal, current status, acceptance criteria, and the tasks that compose it.
-
-* Goal
-
-Conventions become named convention sets. A set carries a name, a purpose and a description, and a system holds few of them, so a person reads a short list and knows what each one is for. A report binds one set by choosing it. Authoring a set is a separate UX and is addressed outside this story. This story records the gaps that today stop the list from being drawn from the schema, and points at the two report prototypes that show the choosing surface.
-
-* Status
-
-| Field         | Value                                  |
-|---------------+----------------------------------------|
-| State         | BACKLOG                              |
-| Parent sprint | [[id:3CEE598D-47C8-4EC0-9E01-19CE79CCA4CD][Sprint 28]] |
-| Now           | The decision is recorded and the choosing surface is drawn. No schema, service or screen work has started. |
-| Waiting on    | Nothing.                               |
-| Next          | Scope the name, purpose and description columns and the set-to-kind children, then break the story into tasks. |
-| Last touched  | 2026-10-17                               |
-
-* Acceptance
-
-- A convention set has a name, a purpose and a description, and the three are stored, not derived.
-- A system holds few convention sets: few enough that one page lists them all, and each one is clearly named and clearly purposed.
-- A report binds one set by choosing it, and the set it binds is stated on the report and on the configuration it binds.
-- The choosing surface is one page: a row per set carrying its name, its purpose, the number of kinds it covers, and whether it is the set this report uses.
-- A person who finds no set that fits follows one link from that page to the authoring UX. Authoring a set is not part of the report flow.
-- The publish carries a correction to a tenant that already holds the row for all 26 kinds.
-- The conventions configuration a report binds carries its kinds as children, and a run reads the document those children name.
-
-* Prototypes
-
-The choosing surface this story asks for is drawn in two report prototypes,
-and those two pages are the answer to the story:
-
-- [[file:../../../../../prototypes/reporting/create-a-report/][Create a report]] —
-  =doc/prototypes/reporting/create-a-report/=. Step 2, *The conventions it
-  binds*, lists the named sets, states the purpose and the kinds each one
-  covers, marks the one this report uses, and offers the choice as a radio.
-- [[file:../../../../../prototypes/reporting/change-what-a-report-runs/][Change what a report runs]] —
-  =doc/prototypes/reporting/change-what-a-report-runs/=. Step 1 carries the same
-  list for the report being changed, with the same choice and the same link out.
-
-Both pages draw one fixture list and say so. **The authoring prototype is not in
-this MR.** Authoring a set is deferred to its own work, and the deferral is
-recorded in the conventions journeys: the authoring journey states that its
-prototype belongs to that work and not to this one. The link out from a report to
-the authoring UX is drawn and marked as not in this MR.
-
-* Tasks
-
-The story states a decision and the gaps that block it. It breaks into tasks
-once the set's columns and children are scoped.
-
-| Task | State | Start | End | Description |
-|------+-------+-------+-----+-------------|
-|      |       |       |     |             |
-
-* Decisions
-
-- Conventions are named convention sets, not a per-kind table. A person chooses
-  a set; a person does not assemble 26 kinds one at a time in a report.
-- Authoring a set is a separate UX. The report offers two acts only: choose an
-  existing set, or follow the link to the authoring UX.
-- The report prototypes carry no per-kind table, no alternative per kind, no
-  provenance card and no migration state. Those belong to authoring.
-
-* Notes: the gaps that block the list today
-
-Each entry is a fact about the tree at 2026-10-17 and is why the prototypes draw
-fixtures.
-
-- **No name column and no purpose column.** Nothing stores the name of a
-  convention, let alone a purpose. The name a page shows today is derived from
-  the terms of the document in use, and a purpose has no home at all. So the
-  names and purposes in the prototypes are fixtures.
-- **No default marker.** Every kind holds many documents (swap 320, commodity
-  future 790) and no table records which one a run reads. The choice of a set
-  can not yet say which document a kind resolves to.
-- **The configuration carries no children.** =ores_reporting_configurations_tbl=
-  carries a name, a =configuration_type_code= and an =owning_component=, and no
-  rows beneath it. So a conventions configuration binds 26 kinds in name only:
-  it names none of them.
-- **The publish has no update path for 25 of the 26 kinds.** A re-publish
-  inserts where the row is absent and does nothing where it is present, for 25
-  kinds. Only =currency_pair= updates, and its last publish updated 179 rows. A
-  correction can therefore reach 1 kind of the 26 and no more.
-- **The tenant holds the facts that make the list honest.** ACME holds 10,991
-  convention rows across the 26 kinds: 2,155 for the party and 216 held once for
-  the tenant. 25 of the 26 kinds arrived from a data quality publish and =tenor=
-  was copied from the system tenant.
-
-* Out of scope
-
-- The authoring UX: the screen that creates a set, names it, states its purpose
-  and description, and binds the kinds it covers. It is its own work, and it is
-  deferred so that the report surface stays a choice.
-- Per-kind migration inside the reporting group. The prototype that argued it is
-  retired with this story, because it was built on a configuration binding that
-  does not exist.
-- Any change to the conventions database or to the seeders. This story records
-  the decision and the gaps; the schema work is its own.

 * Notes
-* Notes
-
-- The work is done on PR #3479 and verified there: the BFF builds its family
-  tables from a generated TypeScript twin of the registry, and the staging
-  entities gained their missing TypeScript because that branch regenerated the
-  TypeScript facets as well as the C++ and SQL ones. Typecheck passes and the
-  BFF's 779 tests pass on that branch.
-- The PR does not merge: it conflicts with #3474 in
-  =convention_family_registry.py= and =regenerate_convention_family_registry.py=,
-  because both changed the generator. Resolving it means taking main's generator
-  as the base and re-applying the TypeScript rendering, then regenerating and
-  re-running the checks. Do not resolve it by dropping the twin, which would
-  leave the BFF reading a generated file that regeneration deletes.
-- The staging TypeScript gap was not a deliberate exclusion. The staging branch
-  generated the C++ and SQL addresses only and never ran the TypeScript facets,
-  so the fix is to regenerate every facet for a new entity, not to add files by
-  hand.

The rates, equity and fx variants are out of scope: other environments own them.

-| 4 | The six credit types were listed in five places | instrument.hpp, instrument_batch_mapper.cpp | Fixed | One type tuple and one array tuple, a paired fold in the batch mapper, and a static assertion that the tuples line up |

-* Result
-
-DONE. The credit carrier no longer holds a polymorphic payload field.
-
-- =credit_fact_variant.hpp= is deleted and no consumer references it.
-- =credit_instrument_data= holds one typed array per concrete product type, joined to the header by the trade id each row carries flat: =credit_default_swap_instruments=, =index_credit_default_swap_instruments=, =index_credit_default_swap_option_instruments=, =synthetic_cdo_instruments=, =credit_linked_swap_instruments= and =risk_participation_agreement_instruments=.
-- =instrument.hpp= reads those arrays through typed accessors in place of the variant visit, so no reader needs a discriminator.
-- The six credit types have one home: a type tuple, the array tuple it maps to, and a static assertion that the two line up. =fact_rows=, =visit_credit_facts=, =stamp_ids=, =as_credit= and =append_instrument= all follow it, so a type that is not a credit fact is refused at compile time instead of reaching another product's array.
-- =visit_credit_facts= returns =std::optional=, so a carrier that states no fact is told apart from a visitor that answered false, and the import handler reports the empty case instead of failing silently.
-- =domain_instrument_tests.cpp= covers the empty carrier, the false answer, the one-row case and the array lookup.
-- Consumers migrated: =instrument_batch_mapper.cpp=, =credit_instrument_mapper.cpp= and the ORE import execute handler.
-- Left to their owning environments, as agreed: =rates_fact_variant= and =equity_instrument_variant=.
-
-Every local check passes on =linux-clang-release-ninja=. Nineteen passed in one full
-run and =step-consumers= passed on its own once the fleet was up, because it needs
-a running stream to inspect. =ctest= took 1536.3 s and every suite passed. The ORE
-XML round trip passes, which is the evidence that import and export still round
-trip. Base is =origin/main= at =2176c3c1ec=.

 * Result
+
+The accumulator's =RangeBounds= list is a child table. =range_bound= is keyed by
+the trade and the entry's ordinal, holds the optional start date, the four money
+levels as exact decimal and the leverage as a continuous double, and carries the
+two foreign keys the other instrument children carry. =range_bounds_json= is gone
+from the model, the SQL, the domain type, the entity, the protocol, the shell
+command and both mappers, and the hand-written JSON serializer and parser are
+deleted.
+
+The four money levels cross the ORE boundary through =moneyFloat=, so the digits
+the document states reach the decimal column. Two goldens recorded the old
+float spelling and now record the document's own: =1.04999995= became =1.05=,
+=1.10000002= became =1.1=, and a stated =0.0= stays =0.0=.
+
+An accumulator that holds no range bound is refused on export with a stated
+error, because the ORE schema requires at least one and a document without it
+cannot be read back.
+
+The child is keyed by the trade alone, so the equity accumulator can move onto
+the same table in its own unit; it still writes JSON text today.
+
+* Decisions
+
+- *The child is trade-keyed, not FX-keyed.* A =RangeBounds= list belongs to the
+  trade its document states, and the equity accumulator states the same list, so
+  one table serves both. Keying it to the family would duplicate the shape.
+- *Leverage stays a double.* It is a multiplier, not a money amount, so the
+  continuous rule applies and the column is a binary double. The four price
+  levels are money and are exact decimals.
+- *The levels are money leaves in the binding.* =rangeBound='s five levels were
+  plain floats, so the document's digits were lost before the mapper ran. They
+  are =moneyFloat= now, added to the reapply script with the rest of the family.
+- *A stated level the binding never carried is null, not zero.* Every level is
+  optional in the schema, so an absent level is a null column and the reverse
+  mapper writes no element back.
+- *The trailing zero is the one spelling the round trip normalises.* A stated
+  =0.0= reaches a decimal column as zero, so the golden records =0.0= only where
+  the binding carried the text; a value that passes through the decimal writes
+  its canonical spelling.

-This page documents a [[id:F44766FA-1E9C-416F-849A-E131101B2ECA][user journey]]: A person writes a convention that no curated document states, for one kind and one party.
-
-A user journey describes what one person is trying to do, before anything is
-built. It is a design document that outlives any sprint, so it names the
-screens, the entity fields each screen shows, and the operations and messages
-each step needs.
-
-* Goal
-
-"We trade something the convention list does not cover, and the run has to read
-a term set that states it. I want to write that set down once, for my party, and
-be able to show later what it said and who changed it."
-
-The journey is done when the new document exists, its terms are the ones the
-person meant, and its record shows the version, the author, the time and the
-reason. That last part is not paperwork: the terms are copied into a
-conventions file that a run reads, so the record of who wrote them is the record
-of what a run read.
-
-This is a different job from
-[[id:FA1CC25B-9745-4172-BAE8-4B6413958077][Change the convention a party uses
-for one kind]]. There the document already exists and the person picks it or
-corrects it. Here nothing exists — the person is the author of a term set, and
-the curated list is one more thing that was authored before them.
-
-* Actor and trigger
-
-The actor is the person who owns the market terms the desks book on: a market
-risk owner acting inside their own tenant, a tenant administrator, or an
-account holding =Operations=, which holds =refdata::<kind>_conventions:write=
-for every kind. A market risk owner knows the terms and asks for them; an
-operations account holds the write and makes it.
-
-The trigger is a trade whose terms no document states, or a term set the party
-agreed with a counterparty that the curated dataset does not carry. The person
-arrives from the kind's list — having found that the document they need is not
-there — or from a trade whose booking is blocked on it. The journey starts on
-one kind and ends when the new document is saved and its history reads back.
-
-This journey writes one new convention row of one kind. It does not write a
-report definition, a binding, a schedule or a trade, and it does not run
-anything.
-
-The journey keeps no server state. No step waits on the server after its reply.
-
-* Steps
-
-1. *Establish that the terms are not already there.* The person opens the kind
-   and searches for the terms they need. The generated filter takes =id_one_of=
-   and nothing else, so the search is a page of rows read in words, and on a kind
-   of 320 documents it is a real cost. The step exists because authoring a
-   document that duplicates one of the 201 existing term sets is the mistake this
-   journey must not make, and the screen has no cheap way to prevent it. See
-   /What is missing/.
-2. *Choose the kind.* The person picks the convention kind that serves the
-   instrument family they are booking. There are 26 and each is its own table
-   with its own columns, so the kind is chosen before any field is drawn: the
-   screen draws the fields the chosen kind's table carries and no others. A
-   =swap= row states a fixed calendar, a fixed frequency, a fixed convention, a
-   fixed day count, an index, a float frequency and a sub-periods coupon type; a
-   =deposit= row states whether it is index-based and, if not, its own calendar,
-   convention, day count and settlement days.
-3. *Read the fields, and what each one is.* The system shows every term column
-   the kind carries, grouped by the part of the schedule it belongs to, and says
-   of each whether it is a pick from another reference list or a value that lives
-   only on this row. A pick holds the list's code and the screen shows the code
-   and the label. The screen states where the grouping comes from: it is the
-   screen's reading, because the table carries no leg or schedule object.
-4. *Author the terms.* The person fills the fields. Every field the model marks
-   as required is required; every nullable field may be left empty, and the
-   screen shows it as empty rather than defaulting it, because empty and stated
-   are different claims a later reader has to tell apart. A term that is a pick
-   is not created here: the screen links to the list that owns it, and says so.
-5. *Review.* The system shows the term set in the table's own column order, a
-   count of the fields the person filled, and, for each optional column left
-   empty, that it is empty. Nothing is written until the person confirms.
-6. *Save.* The person saves. The system writes the row with one request,
-   =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.put=, carrying the row, a =must_not_exist=
-   precondition and a =change_intent=. The precondition is what makes this safe:
-   a key already present is refused rather than overwriting a document someone
-   else wrote. The intent carries a reason code from =dq.v1.change_reasons.list=
-   and the person's own commentary. The service stamps =modified_by=,
-   =performed_by=, =valid_from= and =valid_to= from the session, and the row's
-   =version= starts at 1.
-7. *See the result.* The system reports the document's key, its version, and what
-   the write did not do: it did not mark the document as one a run takes, because
-   no such mark exists, and it did not attach the document to any report, because
-   a conventions configuration holds no rows to attach it to. What the person has
-   actually done is add a document that every run of the party will now carry.
-8. *Read the record.* The person opens the history. The first version shows the
-   terms as authored, the author, the time and the reason. The bitemporal
-   envelope is what this step is about: a later correction closes this row with a
-   =valid_to= and writes version 2 with a =valid_from=, so this version stays
-   readable, and the two can be compared field by field.
-9. *Leave, or go on.* The person returns to the kind's list, or goes to
-   [[id:FA1CC25B-9745-4172-BAE8-4B6413958077][Change the convention a party
-   uses for one kind]] to correct what they just wrote, or to
-   [[id:0DC107D4-170D-478B-9476-570343806888][See the conventions a party
-   uses]] to read the kind back.

-* Screens and wireframes
-
-One screen: the kind in the header, the fields the kind's table carries grouped
-by the part of the schedule, the review panel, the outcome, and the history as
-the outcome step's own view. The rail shows the steps in order, and the last step
-cannot be returned past.
-
-The screen is a form over one table, because that is what authoring a convention
-is. It draws the fields it reads from the table and invents none: the 26 tables
-have different columns and a screen that drew a single shared form would be
-claiming a shape the data does not have.

-
-No prototype is written for this journey in this pass. The act it describes is a
-form over one table and there is no open interaction question in it, which is
-the condition for spending a prototype; the questions that are open here are
-about the server and are recorded in /What is missing/.
-
-Conventions are named convention sets: a set carries a name, a purpose and a
-description, a system holds few of them, and a report binds one by choosing it.
-Authoring a set is its own UX, and its prototype is deferred to its own work. It
-is not in this MR, and nothing here draws it. The decision, and the gaps that
-block it, are recorded in the story
-[[file:../../../agile/versions/v0/sprint_28/name-the-convention-sets-a-report-chooses/story.org][Name
-the convention sets a report chooses]] (DE6C0BDA-D12A-4E31-AA86-C323F5A7E016).
-The report side of the choice is drawn in
-[[file:../../prototypes/reporting/create-a-report/][Create a report]] and
-[[file:../../prototypes/reporting/change-what-a-report-runs/][Change what a
-report runs]], and those two pages are the choosing surface this journey feeds.
-
-* Entities composed
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Entity | What it contributes | Model |
-|--------+---------------------+-------|
-| The kind's convention table | The row this journey writes: every term column of the chosen kind, plus =version=, =valid_from=, =valid_to=, =modified_by=, =performed_by=, =change_reason_code= and =change_commentary= | one of the 26; see below |
-| =change_reason= | The reason code the person supplies, from the tenant's own list | |
-| =calendar_name=, =day_count_fraction_type=, =business_day_convention_type=, =payment_frequency=, =floating_index_type=, =sub_period_coupon_type= | The lists a pick is a code from | |
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Entity | What it contributes | Model |
-|--------+---------------------+-------|
-| =swap_convention= | The worked example: seven term columns, of which five are picks and two are required text | [[id:F68E18C5-A704-40E8-A37B-4B8F5DCB5089][ores.refdata.swap_convention]] |
-| =deposit_convention= | The contrast: =index_based= decides whether the row states its own terms or inherits them, so the same kind draws two shapes | [[id:F7C5287B-7781-45EA-BA4C-63F077E36A89][ores.refdata.deposit_convention]] |
-| =ibor_index_convention= | The tenant kind: a document authored here belongs to no party, so it is authored once for the tenant | [[id:852FE06C-70D9-48BC-B768-D99D87D0D796][ores.refdata.ibor_index_convention]] |
-| =overnight_index_convention= | The same, for the overnight index | [[id:B72547F3-83B5-4F83-AA65-BBE16C191089][ores.refdata.overnight_index_convention]] |
-| =tenor_convention= | The one kind with a description column, and the one kind keyed by =code= | [[id:C4D8A2E6-3B7F-4A1D-9C5E-8F2A6D3B1E90][ores.refdata.tenor_convention]] |
-| =currency_pair_convention= | The tenant kind keyed by =pair_code=, whose calendars are a child table | [[id:1B88215B-1FE0-4CAF-B6AB-53F471963CA6][ores.refdata.currency_pair_convention]] |
-| =party= | The owner of a document authored on one of the 22 party kinds | [[id:8F3A1C2D-4B5E-4A6C-8F9D-2E3F4A5B6C7D][ores.refdata.party]] |
-
-The writable fields are the table's own columns and nothing else. The row's key
-is =id= on 24 kinds, =code= on =tenor= and =pair_code= on =currency_pair=, and
-the person supplies it: nothing generates a key, and the key is what a
-conventions file refers to a document by.
-
-The envelope is the table's, not a separate store. =version= starts at 1,
-=valid_from= is the write's time, =valid_to= is the store's infinity until the
-next version closes it, =modified_by= and =performed_by= come from the session,
-and =change_reason_code= with =change_commentary= come from the request. The
-convention tables are the only record of who wrote a term and why.
-
-* Operations and messages
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Step | Operation | Subject | Status |
-|------+-----------+---------+--------|
-| Establish that it is not there | List the kind's documents | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.list= | exists |
-| Establish that it is not there | Read one document | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.get= | exists |
-| Author the terms | Fill the calendar picker | =refdata.v1.calendar_names.list= | exists |
-| Author the terms | Fill the day count picker | =refdata.v1.day_count_fraction_types.list= | exists |
-| Author the terms | Fill the business-day convention picker | =refdata.v1.business_day_convention_types.list= | exists |
-| Author the terms | Fill the payment frequency picker | =refdata.v1.payment_frequencies.list= | exists |
-| Author the terms | Fill the floating index picker | =refdata.v1.floating_index_types.list= | exists |
-| Save | Offer the change reasons | =dq.v1.change_reasons.list= | exists |
-| Save | Write the new document | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.put= (=must_not_exist=) | exists |
-| Read the record | List the document's versions | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions_versions.list= | exists |
-| Read the record | Read one version | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions_versions.get= | exists |
-| Read the record | Read every version with its diff | =refdata.v1.history.get= (=entity_type= = =ores.refdata.<kind>_convention=) | exists |
-| See the result | Announce the write | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions_events.created= | exists |
-| Establish that it is not there | Search the kind by a term | (the filter is =id_one_of= and nothing else) | missing |
-| Attach the document to a report | Record which document a run takes | (no default column, no default row) | missing |
-| The screen itself | Author a convention from the browser | (no BFF route) | missing |
-
-The per-kind subjects are the generated ones: =refdata.v1.swap_conventions.put=,
-=refdata.v1.tenor_conventions.put=, =refdata.v1.currency_pair_conventions.put=
-and their equals. =swap_conventions_versions.list= and =.get= read the versions
-of one document; =refdata.v1.history.get= reads them with a diff.
-
-No BFF route serves conventions. This journey adds one, for example
-=POST /api/refdata/parties/<party-id>/conventions/<kind>=, which validates the
-person's terms against the term lists, sends the =put= with =must_not_exist=,
-and returns the new key and version.
-
-* What is missing
-
-1. *The new document is indistinguishable from 320 others.* A row is authored
-   with a key the person chose and no name or description, so nothing a reader
-   sees says what it is for. The only kind with a description column is =tenor=.
-   The screen derives a name from the terms, and a derived name collides: the
-   party already holds 201 distinct term sets across 320 swap rows. The person
-   who authors the 202nd has authored a document a reader cannot pick out by
-   name.
-2. *Nothing prevents authoring a duplicate of a document already there.* The
-   precondition is =must_not_exist= on the key, so a new key with terms identical
-   to an existing row is accepted. Finding the duplicate first needs a term
-   search the list does not offer, so the check is a person reading 320 rows.
-3. *The new document is not marked as the one a run takes.* Authoring adds a row
-   to the party's conventions document, and the export writes every row of that
-   document. So the run reads the new document and reads the 320 old ones equally
-   and has no way to be told which applies. A default marker is the missing
-   piece, exactly as it is for
-   [[id:FA1CC25B-9745-4172-BAE8-4B6413958077][Change the convention a party uses
-   for one kind]].
-4. *A refused write carries no field-level record.* A =must_not_exist= violation
-   or a term naming a value the list no longer holds arrives as a plain error
-   with a code and a message, and the screen has to name the offending field
-   itself.
-5. *No convention field validates its term.* The models declare no foreign key
-   and no lookup check on a convention's term columns, so the server stores any
-   text and a term list that no longer holds a code does not refuse the write.
-6. *The history has no draft version.* =refdata.v1.history.get= returns saved
-   versions only, so the history view is a post-write view and a person cannot
-   compare what they are about to write against what is stored.
-7. *An authored document does not travel.* There is no route from a tenant's
-   authored row back into the curated DQ dataset, so a term a party needs is
-   authored again in every tenant, and the next publish cannot carry it. The DQ
-   tables are seeded in the system tenant and published downward; nothing writes
-   a tenant's row upward.
-8. *A tenant-scoped kind is authored for the whole tenant.* Authoring a
-   =currency_pair=, =ibor_index=, =overnight_index= or =tenor= document writes a
-   row no party owns, so it is one document for every party of the tenant. The
-   screen states the scope; nothing refuses the write on that ground.
-9. *No four-eyes control is seeded.* A new term set that every desk's runs will
-   read cannot be second-checked: the approval operations exist, no request kind
-   is seeded for a convention, and nothing applies a change when the last decider
-   approves.

-#+title: User Journey: Change the convention a party uses for one kind
-#+description: A person finds the one convention of one kind that states a term wrongly, chooses a different document or corrects the row, and reads what the change reaches, which is every run of the party and not one report.
-#+type: user_journey
-#+level: cross
-#+filetags: :knowledge:user_journey:refdata:reporting:
-#+created: 2026-10-18
-#+updated: 2026-10-18

-
-This page documents a [[id:F44766FA-1E9C-416F-849A-E131101B2ECA][user journey]]: A person changes one convention of one kind for one party, and reads what the change reaches.
-
-A user journey describes what one person is trying to do, before anything is
-built. It is a design document that outlives any sprint, so it names the
-screens, the entity fields each screen shows, and the operations and messages
-each step needs.
-
-* Goal
-
-"The AED swaps are being booked on 30/360 and they should be ACT/360. I want to
-change that one thing, and I want to know what it hits before I do it."
-
-The person has one kind and one wrong term. The journey is done when the terms
-of that kind state what the person meant, they know which runs will read the new
-terms and which will not, and they know whether the change reached their party
-alone or the whole tenant.
-
-"Choosing a different document" and "correcting a document" are the same act on
-this screen and different acts on the server, and the screen says which one it
-is about to send. Choosing a different document is picking an existing row;
-correcting a document is writing a new version of that row. The third act, a
-term no document states, is not this journey:
-[[id:857206FA-DA09-4920-8713-D28E613C8BCC][Author a convention for a kind]] is.
-
-* Actor and trigger
-
-The actor is the person who maintains the tenant's reference data for the desks:
-an account holding =Operations=, which holds =refdata::<kind>_conventions:read=
-and =refdata::<kind>_conventions:write= for every kind, or a tenant
-administrator, who holds =*= and can also reach the operations no other role
-holds.
-
-The trigger is a trade or a run whose terms are wrong. The person arrives from
-[[id:0DC107D4-170D-478B-9476-570343806888][See the conventions a party uses]],
-having found the kind and read its terms, or from a run whose figures are
-doubted. The journey starts on one kind of one party and ends when the person
-has read the reach.
-
-This journey writes one convention row of one kind. It does not write a report
-definition, its bindings or its schedule, and it does not run a report. The next
-run of a definition carries the change; nothing here makes one.
-
-The journey keeps no server state. No step waits on the server after its reply.
-
-* Steps
-
-1. *Open the kind.* The person arrives with one kind and one party already
-   chosen and lands on that kind's documents, not on the 26-kind list. The
-   system shows the kind's name, how many term columns its table carries, how
-   many documents the party holds, and whether the party or the tenant owns them.
-   The scope is stated on this step and not in a footnote, because it decides
-   who a write reaches: 22 kinds belong to the party and four belong to the
-   tenant.
-2. *Find the document that states the wrong term.* The person filters the kind's
-   documents. The generated filter takes =id_one_of= and nothing else, so the
-   field says on screen that it filters by key, and it cannot be used to ask for
-   "the AED swaps". The screen offers the two reads that work: page the list and
-   filter in the client, or open the document whose key the person already holds.
-   The terms are shown in words beside each row so the person can find the wrong
-   one by reading, which is the only search that reaches 320 documents.
-3. *Read what the row states, and what it inherits.* The system opens the row.
-   Every term column the table carries is shown, grouped by the part of the
-   schedule it belongs to. A term that is a pick from another reference list
-   holds that list's code and never its label, and the screen shows the code and
-   the label and says which list owns it. A term the row leaves empty is shown
-   as empty and not as a value, because empty and stated are different claims.
-   For =deposit_convention= the screen reads =index_based= first: when it is
-   set, the row states no calendar, convention, day count or settlement days and
-   inherits them from the index, so the person is told they are about to edit
-   columns a run does not read.
-4. *Choose which act this is.* The screen offers two, and never presents them as
-   one button. *Use a different document* picks another existing row of the same
-   kind. *Correct this document* writes a new version of this row with the
-   person's terms. The person picks, and the summary states which one is staged.
-   Nothing is written until they confirm.
-5. *Confirm the change and see the reach before the write.* The system shows what
-   will change: every field in the table's own order, a count of the fields that
-   differ from the version it read, and the reach. The reach is stated in three
-   sentences and each is a fact:
-   - *It reaches every definition of this party.* The conventions file a run is
-     assembled from is written from the party's whole conventions document, and
-     the configuration the definition binds is not read to build it. So the
-     change reaches all 22 of ACCOUS's definitions. On a tenant-scoped kind it
-     reaches every party of the tenant.
-   - *The reach looks narrower than it is, and that is the danger.* In ACME each
-     party binds one conventions configuration for all of its definitions —
-     ACCOUS 22 definitions on *US conventions*, ACCOUK 24 on *UK conventions*,
-     ACCOHK 22 on *HK conventions*, ACMCOR 10 on *Group conventions*. So the
-     party's reach and the configuration's reach coincide and a person never sees
-     the difference. Where a party bound two conventions configurations the
-     change would still reach both, and the screen would have said it reached one.
-   - *It does not reach a run already produced.* A run keeps the file it ran
-     with, and its outputs and its errors are that run's own record.
-   - *Nothing records which run read which version.* The comparison a reader
-     makes across the change is a comparison of two different sets of terms, and
-     the person cannot name the runs on the far side of it.
-6. *Write.* The person saves. The system writes the row with one request,
-   =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.put=, carrying the change, a precondition and
-   the intent. A correction states =must_match_version= with the version it read,
-   so a concurrent edit is refused instead of overwritten; a new document states
-   =must_not_exist=. Choosing a different document writes nothing for that
-   reason: both documents already exist. What the person has actually staged
-   there is a default, and there is no default to write — see /What is missing/.
-7. *See the result, and read what the write did not do.* The system reports the
-   document's new version, when it was written, by whom and with which change
-   reason. It also states the two things the write did not do: it did not mark
-   the document as the one a run takes, because no such mark exists; and it did
-   not retire the document it replaced, because a convention is retired by a
-   delete and this journey sends none.
-8. *Read the versions.* The person opens the history and reads every saved
-   version with the field-level difference from the one before. A revert is not a
-   history operation: it reads the old version and writes its values as a new
-   version, through the same =put= with a new change reason.
-9. *Leave, or go on.* The person returns to the kind's list, to the conventions
-   table, or runs the report to see the new terms take effect. The run is
-   [[id:76431668-8656-4276-9F9B-F292FE45B2CA][Run a report and watch it
-   finish]]'s page.
-
-* Screens and wireframes
-
-One screen: the kind in the header, the documents on the left, the open document
-and its terms on the right, and the reach as a panel the person must read before
-the confirm enables. The screen writes one row and reads the rest.
-
-The reach panel is not decoration. A person who believes they are changing one
-report's conventions and is in fact changing every run of the party has been
-misled by a screen, and this one does not do that.
-

-document of a kind a run takes, cannot be drawn as a working interaction when
-the server has nowhere to put the choice: a screen that staged one would be
-drawing a write that fails.
-

-authoring, which has its own UX and is deferred. No prototype here draws a
-per-kind table or a choice per kind. The decision, and the missing default
-marker, are recorded in the story

-The models the rest of this group leans on:
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading

-|--------+---------------------+-------|
-| =swap_convention= | The worked example: seven term columns, and the row a person is most likely to be correcting | [[id:F68E18C5-A704-40E8-A37B-4B8F5DCB5089][ores.refdata.swap_convention]] |

-| =ibor_index_convention= | The tenant kind whose row a party edit changes for every party | [[id:852FE06C-70D9-48BC-B768-D99D87D0D796][ores.refdata.ibor_index_convention]] |
-| =overnight_index_convention= | The same, for the overnight index | [[id:B72547F3-83B5-4F83-AA65-BBE16C191089][ores.refdata.overnight_index_convention]] |
-| =tenor_convention= | The tenant kind with a description column and no DQ route | [[id:C4D8A2E6-3B7F-4A1D-9C5E-8F2A6D3B1E90][ores.refdata.tenor_convention]] |
-| =currency_pair_convention= | The tenant kind keyed by the pair rather than by an id | [[id:1B88215B-1FE0-4CAF-B6AB-53F471963CA6][ores.refdata.currency_pair_convention]] |
-| =party= | The owner of the 22 party kinds, and the party the export resolves | [[id:8F3A1C2D-4B5E-4A6C-8F9D-2E3F4A5B6C7D][ores.refdata.party]] |
-
-Every one of these tables is bitemporal. A write does not overwrite: it closes
-the current row with a =valid_to= and writes the next version with a
-=valid_from=, so the version a run read stays readable. The =change_reason_code=
-and =change_commentary= the person supplies are stored on the row, and
-=modified_by= and =performed_by= are derived from the session and not from the
-request.

-* Operations and messages
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Step | Operation | Subject | Status |
-|------+-----------+---------+--------|
-| Open the kind | List the kind's documents | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.list= | exists |
-| Find the document | Read one document | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.get= | exists |
-| Find the document | Read several by key | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.get_many= | exists |
-| Read the terms | Fill the term pickers | =refdata.v1.calendar_names.list=, =refdata.v1.day_count_fraction_types.list=, =refdata.v1.business_day_convention_types.list=, =refdata.v1.payment_frequencies.list=, =refdata.v1.floating_index_types.list= | exists |
-| Confirm the change | Offer the change reasons | =dq.v1.change_reasons.list= | exists |
-| The reach | Read the party's definitions | =reporting.v1.report_definitions.list= | exists |
-| The reach | Read the configurations they bind | =reporting.v1.report_configurations.list= | exists |
-| The reach | Read the conventions configurations | =reporting.v1.configurations.list_by_configuration_type_code= | exists |
-| Write | Correct the document | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.put= (=must_match_version=) | exists |
-| Write | Add a document | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.put= (=must_not_exist=) | exists |
-| Read the versions | List the document's versions | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions_versions.list= | exists |
-| Read the versions | Read every version with its diff | =refdata.v1.history.get= (=entity_type= = =ores.refdata.<kind>_convention=) | exists |
-| See the result | Learn that a convention changed | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions_events.updated= | exists |
-| Retire a document | Close a document a run should stop reading | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.delete= | exists, not offered by this journey |
-| Choose which document a run takes | Mark one document of a kind as the one in use | (no default column, no default row) | missing |
-| Search the kind by a term | Filter the list by anything but the key | (the filter is =id_one_of= and nothing else) | missing |
-| The screen itself | Change a convention from the browser | (no BFF route) | missing |
-
-The per-kind subjects are the generated ones: =refdata.v1.swap_conventions.put=,
-=refdata.v1.deposit_conventions.put=, =refdata.v1.ibor_index_conventions.put=
-and their equals for the rest. A tenant kind's key holds no party:
-=refdata.v1.ibor_index_conventions.put= takes an =id= and no party.
-
-The =delete= exists and this journey does not send it. Retiring a document a run
-reads is a different decision from correcting it, and nothing checks that a
-document is unreferenced before it is closed.
-
-No BFF route serves conventions. This journey adds the write behind the route the
-reading journey adds, for example =PUT
-/api/refdata/parties/<party-id>/conventions/<kind>/<key>=, which reads the row's
-current version, sends the =put= with =must_match_version=, and returns the new
-version.
-
-* What is missing
-
-1. *Choosing a different document has nothing to write to.* The journey's first
-   act, "use a different document", is the act the person most often wants, and
-   the server has no place for it. There is no default column on any of the 26
-   tables and no per-kind default row keyed by tenant and kind. Choosing a
-   different document would therefore be a write that changes nothing a run
-   reads. A default needs one of the two shapes, and until one exists this
-   journey cannot be built past step 4.
-2. *The change reaches more than the screen can promise to narrow.* The
-   conventions file a run is assembled from is written from the party's whole
-   conventions document; the bound configuration's id is not read. So a person
-   who corrects one swap document changes what every definition of the party
-   reads. The screen states it, and stating it does not fix it: there is no
-   server-side way to scope the change to one report, and no server-side way to
-   scope it to one kind's documents either, because the document write replaces
-   the party's rows kind by kind in one call. The gap is hidden in ACME, where
-   each party binds one conventions configuration and the two scopes coincide,
-   so the defect is invisible until a tenant wants two.
-3. *The list cannot be searched by a term.* The generated filter accepts
-   =id_one_of= and nothing else. On a kind of 320 documents, a person who knows
-   the term and not the key cannot find the row. A term filter on each list is
-   the missing operation, and it is the same gap
-   [[id:0DC107D4-170D-478B-9476-570343806888][See the conventions a party
-   uses]] records.
-4. *No operation says whether a document is in use.* Nothing joins a convention
-   row to a run, a trade or a definition, so the screen cannot warn that the
-   document about to be corrected is one something reads. The best it can do is
-   say that every document of the party is read by every run.
-5. *A refused write carries no field-level record.* The refusal this journey must
-   handle is a term that references a value its list no longer holds, and the
-   generated =result= carries no =field_failure= for a convention service, so the
-   server cannot name the field it refused and the screen must match the code and
-   the message itself.
-6. *No convention field validates its term.* A convention's term columns are
-   plain text with no foreign key and no lookup check declared on the model, so
-   the server stores any text. A term that references a value the list does not
-   hold is written rather than refused, and the run is where it shows up.
-7. *A tenant-scoped kind is changed for the whole tenant with no warning.* Four
-   kinds carry no =party_id=: =currency_pair=, =ibor_index=, =overnight_index=
-   and =tenor=. A person correcting the IBOR index conventions for their own
-   party is changing 10 rows the whole tenant reads. The screen can say so
-   because the table's shape says so; nothing in the server reports the scope
-   back, and the write is refused by no one.
-8. *The whole-document write is a second, wider write to the same rows.*
-   =refdata.v1.conventions_documents.put= writes every kind of the party's
-   document in one call, and it leaves rows it is not given alone, so it can
-   neither delete nor retire. A person holding =TenantAdmin= can therefore send a
-   document that changes many kinds at once and receives no warning and no
-   summary of what moved. The per-kind =put= is the narrower act and is the one
-   this journey sends; the wider one existing beside it is the hazard.
-9. *No four-eyes control is seeded for a convention change.* The approval
-   operations exist, and no request kind is seeded for a convention row, a
-   request holds no pending change, and nothing applies the change when the last
-   decider approves. A person changing a term every desk reads cannot be
-   second-checked today.
-10. *No run records the version of a convention it read.* The history view says
-    what changed and not which run was affected, so the reach panel's third
-    sentence is a gap and not a warning.
-

-#+title: User Journey: Onboard a party and verify its conventions
-#+description: A tenant administrator provisions a party, reads that its conventions arrive in the same run and are not a manual step, and verifies what landed, what was skipped because the tenant already held it, and what a party the bundle never reached would read.
-#+type: user_journey
-#+level: cross
-#+filetags: :knowledge:user_journey:refdata:tenancy:
-#+created: 2026-10-18
-#+updated: 2026-10-18
-#+startup: inlineimages
-
-This page documents a [[id:F44766FA-1E9C-416F-849A-E131101B2ECA][user journey]]: A tenant administrator verifies that a newly provisioned party has the conventions its runs will read.
-
-A user journey describes what one person is trying to do, before anything is
-built. It is a design document that outlives any sprint, so it names the
-screens, the entity fields each screen shows, and the operations and messages
-each step needs.
-
-* Goal
-
-"I have just provisioned a party. Its runs need market terms from the first
-minute. Do they have them, and how would I know if they did not?"
-
-This journey is a verification and not a fill. A party's conventions are not
-something a person assembles: the provisioning run publishes the
-=party_essentials= bundle once per party, and that bundle's first member is the
-conventions dataset. So the correct answer to "how do I give the new party its
-conventions" is "you do not — the run did it". The journey exists because a
-person still needs to prove it, and because the one state that goes wrong here
-goes wrong silently.
-
-The journey is done when the person can state, for the party they just created,
-how many documents of each kind it holds, which of those belong to the tenant
-rather than the party, and what a run of that party would write today.
-
-* Actor and trigger
-
-The actor is a tenant administrator, or the person operating provisioning for
-the tenant. They hold the tenant's permissions in full and they act inside their
-own tenant. The trigger is a party that has just been created — by a starting
-point's =provision_party= operation, by the Acme demo profile, or by an
-administrator creating one outside a plan — and a run that either has not been
-made yet or has produced figures nobody has checked.
-
-The journey starts when the party exists and ends when the person has read its
-conventions back, or has found that it has none and knows what would fill them.
-
-This is a verification journey. In the normal case it writes nothing: the party
-provisioning already wrote the rows. It reaches one write only in the abnormal
-case, and only by handing the work to
-[[id:99481EA8-1D2B-426D-A4E6-5E834FF5FFCE][Publish conventions from data
-quality]], which is the same publish the provisioning run made.
-
-The journey keeps no server state. The provisioning run does: it is a workflow
-instance, and its steps are where the person reads what the run actually did.
-
-* Steps
-
-1. *Read that the conventions are part of provisioning, and not a step after it.*
-   The person opens the provisioning run and reads the party plan's step 30,
-   =provision_party=, whose argument is ={"bundles": ["party_essentials"]}=. The
-   bundle states what it carries: "The reference data a single party needs: its
-   instrument conventions and its CRM topology. Published once per party with a
-   ={"party_id": "..."}= param." The person reads that the conventions and the CRM
-   topology are the same operation, and that neither is a manual fill. In the
-   Acme demo profile the four operational parties reach this step through the
-   same plan, after the LEI hierarchy import and before staff are loaded.
-2. *Read the publish the plan's step performs, and in what order.* The bundle
-   publishes its members in dependency order, one workflow step per dataset. The
-   conventions dataset, =ore.conventions=, is the bundle's member at display
-   order 5, before the CRM topology at 20. The step's command subject is
-   =refdata.v1.ops.publish_conventions_from_dq= and its parameters carry the
-   party's id. The person reads the step's counts, not a summary: the first
-   party's publish writes 2,188 rows, and every later party's publish writes
-   2,155 and skips 33.
-3. *Read the 33 as already-present and not as a failure.* 2,188 is 2,155 plus 33.
-   The 33 are the tenant-scoped kinds that the first party's publish wrote:
-   =ibor_index= with 10 and =overnight_index= with 23. They carry no =party_id=,
-   so they are the tenant's rows and every later party's publish correctly finds
-   them present. A person who reads 33 without this account reads a defect. The
-   screen states the two kinds and the two counts beside the skip.
-4. *Read the party's own total against what it should be.* The person reads the
-   party's conventions back, kind by kind. A party published from the bundle
-   holds 2,155 rows across the 22 party kinds, and reads a further 216 across the
-   four tenant kinds — =currency_pair= 179, =overnight_index= 23, =ibor_index= 10
-   and =tenor= 4 — which belong to the tenant and are shared with every other
-   party. So the party's own count and the number of documents a run of that
-   party reads are different numbers, and the screen shows both.
-5. *Read why the tenant kinds were there before the party was.* Of the four,
-   two arrived differently from the rest and the person reads why.
-   - =currency_pair= is published into the tenant by the =base= bundle, which is
-     a tenant publication and not a party one, so its 179 rows exist before any
-     party is provisioned.
-   - =tenor='s 4 rows are not published at all. They are copied from the system
-     tenant by =ores_iam_provision_tenant_fn= when the tenant is created, with
-     =system.new_record= and the commentary "Copied from the system tenant during
-     provisioning", and they are never refreshed afterwards.
-   The screen states which of the four came from where, because "the run did it"
-   is true of 2,155 of the rows and of none of the 33's second and later parties.
-6. *Read what a run of this party would write today.* The person asks the
-   question the party was provisioned to answer: what file does a run of this
-   party carry? The export reads the party's whole conventions document, kind by
-   kind, and writes it as the run's =conventionsFile=. For a party published from
-   the bundle that file holds the party's 2,155 rows and the tenant's 216. The
-   person reads that the four conventions configurations ACME's definitions bind
-   do not enter into it, and that every definition of the party writes the same
-   file.
-7. *Read the one party that has nothing, and what that means.* The person creates
-   a party outside the plan, or reads a party whose =provision_party= step failed.
-   It holds nothing for the 22 party kinds, because the bundle's publish never
-   ran for it. It still reads the tenant's 216 for the four tenant kinds, so the
-   party is not empty and the emptiness is easy to miss. Its runs write a
-   =conventionsFile= with no rows for 22 kinds. Nothing in the tree refuses such
-   a run and nothing says the party was skipped. This is the state the journey
-   exists to catch, and the screen marks it plainly rather than drawing an empty
-   table with no explanation.
-8. *Fill the gap with the operation provisioning already used, not with a
-   hand-written set.* The person who has to fix a party nobody published for
-   sends the same publish provisioning sends:
-   =dq.v1.ops.publish_bundle= for =party_essentials= with the party's id, or the
-   dataset alone with =dq.v1.ops.publish_datasets=. That publish writes the
-   2,155 rows and reads the 33 as skips, exactly as it does inside provisioning.
-   The person does not author 2,155 rows and does not choose documents:
-   [[id:99481EA8-1D2B-426D-A4E6-5E834FF5FFCE][Publish conventions from data
-   quality]] owns that act and this journey hands to it.
-9. *Leave, or go on.* The party is verified. The person either reads its
-   conventions in detail
-   ([[id:0DC107D4-170D-478B-9476-570343806888][See the conventions a party
-   uses]]), or corrects a term the party needs differently from the curated set
-   ([[id:FA1CC25B-9745-4172-BAE8-4B6413958077][Change the convention a party
-   uses for one kind]]).
-
-* Screens and wireframes
-
-One screen: the party and the provisioning run in the header, the publish step
-with its four counts, and the per-kind read of what the party holds and what it
-shares with the tenant. The state that matters is drawn once and drawn plainly:
-a party with no party-scoped conventions is marked as unpublished, with what a
-run would write and which operation would fill it.
-
-The screen does not offer a hand-entry path for the 2,155 rows. A screen that
-offered one would be teaching a person to do by hand what the plan does, which
-is how a party ends up with 2,155 rows that match no dataset and no provenance.
-
-#+caption: Onboard a party and verify its conventions: the provisioning run's publish step with its counts, the party's 2,155 own rows against the tenant's 216 shared ones, and the party the plan never reached with what a run would write.
-#+attr_html: :width 100%
-[[proj:doc/knowledge/journeys/conventions/wireframe_onboard_a_party_s_conventions.png]]
-
-* Prototype
-
-No prototype is written for this journey in this pass. The journey is a
-verification and its open questions are all about reads the server does not
-offer — a per-party expected count, a record that a party's conventions were
-published, and an attribution of the skip count. A prototype would draw three
-panels and fake all three numbers.
-
-What a prototype must draw when the reads exist is stated here: the publish
-step's four counts, the party's own total beside the tenant's shared total, the
-per-kind table with the owning scope marked, and the unpublished party as its own
-state with the operation that fills it.
-
-* Entities composed
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Entity | What it contributes | Model |
-|--------+---------------------+-------|
-| The 26 convention tables | What the party holds. 22 carry =party_id=; four do not, and a party reads the tenant's rows for those. | one per kind; see below |
-| =report_definition= | The definitions whose next run reads the file, and the party the export resolves | [[id:FB4A11C5-07EA-4923-B8AC-65F46EBA517C][ores.reporting.report_definition]] |
-| =party= | The party being verified, its short code and its parent | [[id:8F3A1C2D-4B5E-4A6C-8F9D-2E3F4A5B6C7D][ores.refdata.party]] |
-| =change_reason= | =system.external_data_import= for a published row and =system.new_record= for a copied one, which tells the two apart after the fact | |
-| =dataset_bundle=, =dataset_bundle_member= | The =party_essentials= bundle and its members, which is what decision "the run does this" rests on | |
-
-The two counts a party has, and why they are different:
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Scope | Kinds | Rows | Written by |
-|-------+-------+------+-----------|
-| The party's own | 22 | 2,155 | =refdata.v1.ops.publish_conventions_from_dq=, once per party, inside =party_essentials= |
-| Shared with the tenant | 4 | 216 | =currency_pair= 179 by the =base= bundle; =overnight_index= 23 and =ibor_index= 10 by the first party's publish; =tenor= 4 by the tenant provisioner |
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Entity | What it contributes | Model |
-|--------+---------------------+-------|
-| =swap_convention= | The kind a person checks first: 320 rows per party | [[id:F68E18C5-A704-40E8-A37B-4B8F5DCB5089][ores.refdata.swap_convention]] |
-| =deposit_convention= | 163 rows per party | [[id:F7C5287B-7781-45EA-BA4C-63F077E36A89][ores.refdata.deposit_convention]] |
-| =ibor_index_convention= | One of the two tenant kinds whose rows the first party's publish writes | [[id:852FE06C-70D9-48BC-B768-D99D87D0D796][ores.refdata.ibor_index_convention]] |
-| =overnight_index_convention= | The other one | [[id:B72547F3-83B5-4F83-AA65-BBE16C191089][ores.refdata.overnight_index_convention]] |
-| =tenor_convention= | The kind no publish reaches, copied by the tenant provisioner | [[id:C4D8A2E6-3B7F-4A1D-9C5E-8F2A6D3B1E90][ores.refdata.tenor_convention]] |
-| =currency_pair_convention= | The kind the =base= bundle publishes before any party exists | [[id:1B88215B-1FE0-4CAF-B6AB-53F471963CA6][ores.refdata.currency_pair_convention]] |
-
-The party-scoped kinds are party-scoped by row-level security, so a party
-session reads its own rows and a tenant administrator reads the tenant's parties.
-That is why the verification screen can be one screen for both actors: the rows
-are the same rows and the policy is what narrows them.
-
-* Operations and messages
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Step | Operation | Subject | Status |
-|------+-----------+---------+--------|
-| Read the plan | Read the provisioning profile's steps | =iam.v1.seed_profile_steps.list= | exists |
-| Read the plan | Read the party-focused bundles | =dq.v1.dataset_bundles.list= | exists |
-| Read the plan | Read a bundle's members | =dq.v1.dataset_bundle_members.list= | exists |
-| Read the publish | Read the run's steps and their results | =workflow.v1.ops.get_workflow_steps= | exists |
-| Read the publish | List the provisioning instances | =workflow.v1.instances.list= | exists |
-| Read the party | List the tenant's parties | =refdata.v1.parties.list= | exists |
-| Verify | List the party's conventions of one kind | =refdata.v1.<kind>_conventions.list= | exists |
-| Verify | Read the party's whole conventions document | =refdata.v1.conventions_documents.get= | exists, not reachable by a person |
-| Verify | Read the party's definitions | =reporting.v1.report_definitions.list= | exists |
-| Fill a party nobody published | Publish the bundle for the party | =dq.v1.ops.publish_bundle= | exists |
-| Fill a party nobody published | Publish the dataset for the party | =dq.v1.ops.publish_datasets= | exists |
-| Verify | Read the party's own total against an expected total | (no read states a party's expected convention count) | missing |
-| Verify | Read that a party's conventions were published | (nothing records it; the workflow step's counts are the only trace) | missing |
-| Verify | Read one publish's counts per kind | (the function returns one total) | missing |
-| The screen itself | Verify a party's conventions from the browser | (no BFF route) | missing |
-
-The provisioning engine dispatches every plan step to one subject,
-=iam.v1.ops.provision_tenant_step=, and the publish operation is one of the
-operations that subject performs. The publish step's own command subject is
-=refdata.v1.ops.publish_conventions_from_dq=, which is what the workflow step
-records and what the person reads.
-
-No BFF route serves this screen. This journey adds one, for example
-=GET /api/refdata/parties/<party-id>/conventions/verification=, which returns
-the party's per-kind counts, the tenant's counts for the four shared kinds, the
-expected total for a party published from =party_essentials=, and the last
-publish step's four counts.
-
-* What is missing
-
-1. *Nothing records that a party's conventions were published.* The publish's
-   only trace is the workflow step's =result_json=, and the conventions rows
-   themselves say =system.external_data_import= whoever wrote them. So the
-   question "did this party's conventions arrive" is answered by counting rows and
-   comparing against a number the person has to know. A per-party marker, or a
-   publication record keyed by party and dataset, would answer it directly.
-2. *No read states a party's expected convention count.* The 2,155 is a fact
-   about the curated dataset, derivable only by counting the artefact tables. A
-   party is verified against a number the person computed elsewhere. No operation
-   returns "this dataset should place these rows for this party".
-3. *A party the plan never reached is indistinguishable from a healthy one at a
-   glance.* It holds 216 tenant rows and no party rows, and every per-kind list
-   answers successfully with no rows. Nothing in the server reports the party as
-   unpublished, so the screen must derive "unpublished" from an empty per-kind
-   list and an expected count it does not have.
-4. *A run for an unpublished party is not refused.* The export writes a
-   conventions file with no rows for the 22 party kinds and the run proceeds. What
-   ORE does with such a file is ORE's affair, and nothing in the tree stops the
-   run or warns the person. A precondition on the run, or a validation at export,
-   is the missing guard.
-5. *The 33 are unattributed on the receipt.* The publish returns one
-   =records_skipped= and the person must know that two tenant-scoped kinds account
-   for it. The same gap
-   [[id:99481EA8-1D2B-426D-A4E6-5E834FF5FFCE][Publish conventions from data
-   quality]] records, seen from the party end.
-6. *`refdata::conventions:read` is held by services and not by the person
-   verifying.* It is held by =OreService= and =ReportRun=, so the one read that
-   answers "what does this party's document hold" is closed to the tenant
-   administrator who is verifying it, and they read 26 lists instead.
-7. *`tenor` is refreshed for no tenant after the first.* Its 4 rows come from a
-   one-time copy at tenant creation. A tenant provisioned before a tenor
-   correction keeps the old rows forever and nothing says so; the only way to
-   refresh them is to write them with the per-kind =put=.
-8. *A starting point other than =acme_demo= may not name the bundle.*
-   =party_essentials= is named by the plans that have one, and a party created
-   outside a plan is published for by nobody. Nothing checks that a party has been
-   through a plan that names the bundle, and nothing reports a party that has not.
