-#+title: User Journey: See a report's results by counterparty
-#+description: A market-risk or credit reader opens one finished run and reads its results by counterparty: each counterparty's aggregate NPV, its notional, its trade count and, where the report runs saccr, its exposure, grouped through the parent counterparty.
-#+type: user_journey
-#+level: cross
-#+filetags: :knowledge:user_journey:reporting:
-#+created: 2026-10-17
-#+updated: 2026-10-17
-#+startup: inlineimages
-
-This page documents a [[id:F44766FA-1E9C-416F-849A-E131101B2ECA][user journey]]: A market-risk or credit reader opens one finished run and reads its results by counterparty: each counterparty's aggregate NPV, its notional, its trade count and, where the report runs saccr, its exposure, grouped through the parent counterparty.
-
-A user journey describes what one person is trying to do, before anything is
-built. It is a design document that outlives any sprint, so it names the
-screens, the entity fields each screen shows, and the operations and messages
-each step needs.
-
-* Goal
-
-"Which counterparties is this run exposed to, and how much of the run is each
-one?" The person has a finished run in front of them and needs the counterparty
-view of it rather than the book view: who the run faces, what each of them is
-worth to it, and which of them carry the concentration. The journey is done
-when they can name the counterparties that dominate the run, hand one of them to
-a colleague with its trades behind the number, and say what the run leaves out.
-
-The book view answers a different question, and
-[[id:969C14D2-4280-4D7C-8F51-1D395B521C83][Read what a run produced]] owns it.
-The same run read by portfolio, book and trade is how a person reconciles their
-own book. Read by counterparty it is how they answer a limit question, a credit
-question, or a desk asking what one name contributed.
-
-* Actor and trigger
-
-Two actors share this journey, and they read it for different reasons. A
-market-risk or credit person reads it after a limit question, or before signing
-off the party's exposure: they need the ranked view, the totals, and the name
-that is out of line. A trading-desk person reads it after a trade or a group of
-trades, asking what one counterparty contributed to the run and which of its
-trades moved the number.
-
-Both act inside their own party. They arrive from a run's row on
-[[id:891DE3CB-2374-4FD9-B7FB-D8892F5174A1][See the reports a party runs]], or
-from the results panel of
-[[id:76431668-8656-4276-9F9B-F292FE45B2CA][Run a report and watch it finish]],
-or from the result of
-[[id:969C14D2-4280-4D7C-8F51-1D395B521C83][Read what a run produced]] by
-switching that result from its book reading to its counterparty reading.
-
-The trigger is a run that has completed, and a question about who it faces. The
-journey starts when the person opens the counterparty view of that run and ends
-when they have the ranked counterparties, or one counterparty's trades, or the
-reason a name they expected is not there.
-
-This is a read-only journey. It reads a run that already exists and changes
-nothing: no run, no definition and no counterparty record.
-
-* Steps
-
-1. *Open the counterparty view of one run.* The person is looking at a completed
-   run, and switches its result from the book reading to the counterparty
-   reading. The view is entered from the run's results, never from a global
-   counterparty list: a counterparty's own page answers "who is this name", and
-   this view answers "what did this run do with this name". The header keeps the
-   run in front of the person, so every figure below is a figure of that run and
-   of no other, and the panel names the analytics the run's report configuration
-   runs, because those decide which measures exist. A report that runs =npv=
-   alone has no exposure column; a report that runs =npv= and =saccr= has both.
-2. *Read the counterparties the run is exposed to.* The screen lists one row per
-   counterparty the run has a result for. Each row states the counterparty's
-   short code and its full name, its aggregate NPV, its notional, its trade
-   count and, where the report runs =saccr=, its exposure. The aggregate NPV is
-   the sum of the =NPV(Base)= of the trades the run attributes to that
-   counterparty, the notional is the sum of those trades' =Notional(Base)=, and
-   the trade count is how many such trades the run holds. The ordering is stated
-   on the screen and is the point of the step: the largest first, by exposure
-   where the report runs =saccr= and by aggregate NPV where it does not. The
-   person scans the top of that list and has the answer to "how much of the run
-   is each one". A share of the run is shown beside the figure, so a row that is
-   a tenth of the run reads as a tenth.
-3. *Group them, because counterparties nest.* A counterparty carries
-   =parent_counterparty_id= on =ores_refdata_counterparties_tbl=, so a banking
-   group and its legal entities are both real, and both are meaningful to
-   different readers: credit reads the group, the desk reads the entity it
-   faces. The screen therefore draws a group and its members as one structure,
-   with the group's own row carrying the sum over its members and each member
-   carrying its own figure. A reader sees a group total and then expands it to
-   the members that make it up, and the total is arithmetic: the group figure is
-   the sum of its members plus the trades booked to the group itself, so a
-   parent that disagrees with its children cannot appear. A counterparty whose
-   parent is not in the run is drawn under a stated heading rather than promoted
-   to a group of one, and a group whose members are all outside the run is drawn
-   as a group with its own trades.
-4. *Open one counterparty.* The person selects a counterparty, and the screen
-   shows what the number is made of: the trades the run attributes to that
-   counterparty, each with its trade id, its trade type, its notional and its
-   NPV, the netting sets those trades sit in, and any error the run recorded
-   against those trades. A trade in the result is the trading trade with that id,
-   so =trading.v1.trades.get= is what resolves the row to the trade itself, and
-   the trade names its =counterparty_id=. The netting set is on the trade's
-   booking, =ores_trading_trade_bookings_tbl=, which carries =trade_id= and
-   =netting_set_id=, so a counterparty's exposure reads by netting set and a
-   person can see which set carries the exposure rather than only the total. The
-   errors are the run's own rows, read by
-   =reporting.v1.report_error_events.list_by_report_instance_id= and filtered to
-   the subjects the counterparty's trades name; their scopes are =Trade=,
-   =Analytics=, =Curve=, =Configuration= and =Report=, and none of them is a
-   counterparty, so a counterparty's errors are reached through its trades and
-   never directly. A person who wants the errors as a set of their own follows
-   [[id:F58B0FB5-3FD8-4BEB-982E-E54D284C0539][Find out why a run went wrong]].
-5. *Notice a name with no result, and a trade with no name.* A counterparty the
-   party can see that the run has no result for is a stated case, not an
-   absence: it is listed with a zero trade count and a dash where the figures
-   would be, and the screen says plainly that the run produced nothing for it.
-   A trade that names no counterparty is the other stated case. The schema
-   allows it: =ores_trading_trades_tbl= carries =counterparty_scope= and a check
-   that =counterparty_id= may be null only when the scope is =intra_entity=, so
-   an intra-entity trade has no counterparty by design. The screen draws such a
-   trade under a stated heading of its own, with its own notional and NPV, and
-   says that the run's counterparty totals are therefore less than the run's
-   total by that amount. Neither case is dropped, because a total that silently
-   leaves out a name or a trade reconciles against nothing.
-6. *Leave, or go on.* The person opens the trades behind one name, follows an
-   error down, opens what the run produced, or goes back to the report's row.
-   The view creates nothing and the next person who opens the run reads the same
-   figures.
-
-No step waits on the server after its reply, and the journey keeps no state of
-its own. It is a run of screens over immediate operations, so it needs no
-[[id:3361CF92-89B0-481E-9E51-ACE2FEEF2FAA][workflow instance]].
-
-* Screens and wireframes
-
-One screen. The run header, the ranked list, the group and member rows, the
-selected counterparty's trades and netting sets, and the errors against them are
-panels of that screen, because they are one answer: what this run faces and how
-much of it each name is. The screen is read-only: it creates nothing, changes
-nothing and destroys nothing.
-
-The list is the screen. A person arrives with a question about concentration and
-leaves with a ranked answer, so the totals, the ordering rule and the share of
-the run each row carries are on the screen and not behind a control. The two
-stated cases sit below the ranked rows rather than inside them, because a name
-with no result is not a measure of zero and a trade with no name is not a
-counterparty.
-
-#+caption: See a report's results by counterparty: the run's ranked counterparties with aggregate NPV, notional, trade count and exposure, a group above its members, one counterparty opened to its trades, netting sets and errors, a counterparty with no result, and a trade that names no counterparty.
-#+attr_html: :width 100%
-[[proj:doc/knowledge/journeys/reporting/wireframe_see_a_reports_results_by_counterparty.png]]
-
-The wireframe draws the three readings the prototype carries as variants: a
-ranked list with a group row above its members and the totals at the foot, a tree
-that expands a group into its members with a rolled-up aggregate at each node,
-and a map of the run as a proportional bar, each segment as wide as its
-counterparty's share, with the selected name read beside it.
-
-* Prototype
-
-The [[file:../../prototypes/reporting/see-a-reports-results-by-counterparty/][prototype]] argues this journey in three interpretations, and [[file:../../prototypes/reporting/see-a-reports-results-by-counterparty.org][its design note]] says what each argues and what is fake. This journey is the design intent for the counterparty view of a run's result, and its prototype belongs at =doc/prototypes/reporting/see-a-reports-results-by-counterparty/=, with hyphens because the inventory gate reads the directory name as a link.
-
-The prototype must draw three structural readings of the same run. =A= draws one
-ranked table, largest first, with a group row above its members and the totals at
-the foot. =B= draws a tree grouped by parent counterparty, each node carrying its
-rolled-up aggregate and expanding to its members, so a group total and its parts
-are visible together. =C= draws a map of the run as a proportional bar, sized by
-each counterparty's NPV, with the selected counterparty read beside it, for the
-person asking how concentrated the run is.
-
-In all three, every counterparty must state its aggregate NPV, its notional, its
-trade count and, where the run's report runs =saccr=, its exposure,
-and every row must carry both the short code and the full name, because a reader
-uses one and recognises the other. Selecting a counterparty must show its trades
-and the errors the run recorded against them. A counterparty with no result and a
-trade that names no counterparty must each be drawn as a stated case rather than
-dropped. A group must be drawn with at least two members, because a group of one
-proves nothing about the roll-up.
-
-Because no operation returns a result grouped by counterparty, and no operation
-parses the run's archive, every figure on the page is a fixture and the panel
-that draws it says so. The panel also states the two facts that make it a
-fixture: nothing parses the archive, and =npv.csv= names the counterparty as a
-name rather than an id.
-
-* Entities composed
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Entity | What it contributes | Model |
-|--------+---------------------+-------|
-| =report_instance= | The run being read: its state, its kind, and the definition it came from. Every figure is a figure of this run | [[id:9FCCF6C8-9C10-403B-BDA4-C3E28706BD67][ores.reporting.report_instance]] |
-| =report_definition= | The definition behind the run, whose report configuration decides which analytics ran and therefore whether there is an exposure column | [[id:FB4A11C5-07EA-4923-B8AC-65F46EBA517C][ores.reporting.report_definition]] |
-| =counterparty= | The row: short code, full name, and =parent_counterparty_id=, which is what makes a group and its members | [[id:8FB6949F-05C1-4867-91F3-B9B6FA2329EC][ores.refdata.counterparty]] |
-| =party_counterparty= | Which counterparties the party can see, so a name with no result can still be listed as a stated case | [[id:77870EE2-3123-4881-AF13-F35D432FC237][ores.refdata.party_counterparty]] |
-| =trade= | The trades behind a counterparty's aggregate: =counterparty_id=, =counterparty_scope=, trade type and notional | [[id:4304A441-E532-45FB-837A-378F13693CAE][ores.trading.trade]] |
-| =netting_set= | The sets the trades sit in, which is the level at which an exposure is reported | [[id:83C9697A-0D6D-42A2-9917-6C68268B5404][ores.refdata.netting_set]] |
-| =report_error_event= | The errors recorded against the trades a counterparty contributed: severity, scope and message | [[id:080B3871-8BAA-4AAA-A98F-3E79F4B83BAA][ores.reporting.report_error_event]] |
-| =report_error_scope= | The vocabulary the errors are placed by, none of whose members is a counterparty | [[id:FF774B04-12E6-4BDF-B94C-222095651C4F][ores.reporting.report_error_scope]] |
-| =party= | The owner of the run and of the counterparty visibility rows | [[id:8F3A1C2D-4B5E-4A6C-8F9D-2E3F4A5B6C7D][ores.refdata.party]] |
-
-The run is the scope; the counterparty is the row. Neither the aggregate NPV, the
-notional, the trade count nor the exposure is a stored field: every one of them
-is derived from the run's result rows and the trades behind them, and *What is
-missing* states the reads that would spare the screen that work. The grouping is
-not stored either: =parent_counterparty_id= is on the counterparty, so the screen
-assembles the tree from the counterparty records it reads.
-
-A trade's netting set is not on the trade. =ores_trading_trades_tbl= carries the
-party, the counterparty and the trade type;
-=ores_trading_trade_bookings_tbl= carries =trade_id=, =book_id= and
-=netting_set_id=, and it versions on its own timeline, so a re-papering into
-another netting set cuts a new version of the booking and leaves the trade alone.
-The screen reads the booking current at the run, which is the booking whose
-window covers the run's start.
-
-The counterparty and the party are party-scoped by row-level security, and the
-run and the definition are bitemporal, so the names the run's own records carry
-are the names of the run and not of today's edit.
-
-* Operations and messages
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Step | Operation | Subject | Status |
-|------+-----------+---------+--------|
-| Open the run's view | Read the run | =reporting.v1.report_instances.get= | exists |
-| Open the run's view | List the runs of a definition, to reach the run | =reporting.v1.report_instances.list= | exists |
-| Open the run's view | Read the run's errors | =reporting.v1.report_error_events.list_by_report_instance_id= | exists |
-| Read the counterparties | List the counterparty records the rows resolve to | =refdata.v1.counterparties.list= | exists |
-| Read the counterparties | Read one counterparty, and its =parent_counterparty_id= | =refdata.v1.counterparties.get= | exists |
-| Read the counterparties | List the counterparties the party can see, so a name with no result can be stated | =refdata.v1.party_counterparties.list_by_party_id= | exists |
-| Read the counterparties | Read the run's results grouped by counterparty | (no operation returns results grouped by counterparty) | missing |
-| Read the counterparties | Read each counterparty's aggregate NPV, notional and trade count | (no operation parses the archive) | missing |
-| Group them | Read a counterparty's parent, and so build the group tree | carried by =refdata.v1.counterparties.list= and =refdata.v1.counterparties.get= | exists |
-| Group them | Roll a group's aggregate up from its members | (the screen sums the rows; no operation rolls up a group) | missing |
-| Open one counterparty | List the trades the run attributes to a counterparty | =trading.v1.trades.list= | exists |
-| Open one counterparty | Read the trade a result row names | =trading.v1.trades.get= | exists |
-| Open one counterparty | List the trades' bookings, and so each trade's =netting_set_id= | =trading.v1.trade_bookings.list= | exists |
-| Open one counterparty | Read the exposure a =saccr= run reported for a netting set | (no operation parses the archive) | missing |
-| Open one counterparty | Read the errors recorded against a counterparty's trades | =reporting.v1.report_error_events.list_by_report_instance_id= | exists |
-| Open one counterparty | Read the errors recorded against a counterparty | (the error scopes carry no counterparty) | missing |
-| Notice a name with no result | List the party's counterparties, to find the ones the run omits | =refdata.v1.party_counterparties.list_by_party_id= | exists |
-| Notice a trade with no name | Find the trades whose =counterparty_id= is null | =trading.v1.trades.list= | exists |
-| The screen itself | Read a run's results by counterparty from the browser | (no BFF route) | missing |
-
-The run, the definition and the errors are reads the reporting service already
-serves. The counterparty records are reference data reads. The trades and their
-bookings are trading reads, and =trades.list= takes a filter record that carries
-=counterparty_id=, so one counterparty's trades in the party are one read rather
-than the whole population filtered in the browser.
-
-The netting sets come free with the reads above: a trade's booking carries
-=netting_set_id=, and the run's own result row carries the netting set's name in
-=NettingSet=. The screen groups a counterparty's exposure by that name and does
-not need the netting set's own record to rank one counterparty against another.
-
-The attribution is the hard part, and it is two joins the platform does not
-serve as one. A result row in =npv.csv= names the counterparty as a name. The
-trade's own =counterparty_id= is the id, reached through
-=trading.v1.trades.get=, and the safety of the join rests on it. Neither the
-group roll-up nor a counterparty's totals is a stored field, so the screen does
-the arithmetic from the result rows and says so.
-
-The reads are gated by =reporting::report_instances:read= and
-=reporting::report_error_events:read= for the run and its errors, and by
-=refdata::counterparties:read= and =trading::trades:read= for the records the
-rows resolve to. The error reads are held by no role below =TenantAdmin= and
-=SuperAdmin=, and those two hold =*=. A credit reader who can see the
-counterparty and its trades therefore cannot read why one of them failed, which
-*What is missing* states rather than paper over.
-
-No BFF route serves reporting. The prototype adds one, for example
-=GET /api/reporting/runs/<run-id>/counterparties=, which returns the run's
-counterparty rows with their aggregates, the grouping, and the stated cases. The
-handler authenticates the caller's token and checks the read codes above.
-
-* What is missing
-
-1. *No operation returns results grouped by counterparty.* The archive holds
-   =npv.csv=, and its columns are exactly =TradeId=, =TradeType=, =Maturity=,
-   =MaturityTime=, =NPV=, =NpvCurrency=, =NPV(Base)=, =BaseCurrency=,
-   =Notional=, =NotionalCurrency=, =Notional(Base)=, =NettingSet= and
-   =CounterParty=. Nothing parses it. =ores_compute_results_tbl= holds the
-   archive's =output_uri=, its =outcome= and its =error_message=, and it holds
-   no parsed rows, so the aggregate NPV, the notional and the trade count of one
-   counterparty have no read behind them, and neither does the exposure a
-   =saccr= run reports. Every figure on this screen waits on a result store or
-   an archive read, and the prototype draws each one as a stated fixture.
-2. *=npv.csv= names the counterparty, it does not identify it.* The file's
-   =CounterParty= column carries a name, and no id. Attributing a result row to
-   a counterparty record therefore needs the trade's =counterparty_id=, which
-   =trading.v1.trades.get= returns, and the netting set the trade sits in, which
-   =trading.v1.trade_bookings.list= returns; the alternative is a match on the
-   name, and a name match is not safe: two legal entities of one group can share
-   a name, =full_name= is not unique in the tenant, and the file's spelling is
-   the engine's rather than the record's. The one thing the name is good for is
-   a warning when it disagrees with the trade's record, and the screen should
-   show that disagreement rather than resolve it silently.
-3. *No read returns a counterparty's errors.* The error model has no counterparty
-   subject: the scopes it places errors by are exactly =Trade=, =Analytics=,
-   =Curve=, =Configuration= and =Report=, so an error is recorded against a
-   trade, an analytic, a curve, the configuration or the run, and never against
-   a counterparty. A counterparty's errors are reached only through the trades
-   that name it, by reading the run's errors and filtering them to the trade ids
-   the counterparty contributed. An error recorded against an analytic alone
-   cannot be attributed to a counterparty at all, and the screen says so instead
-   of dividing it across names.
-4. *No BFF route serves reporting.* Nothing in the web application shows a report
-   today, so the counterparty view is a new route and a new screen as well as a
-   new read.
-5. *No read rolls a group up.* =parent_counterparty_id= is on the counterparty
-   record, and =counterparties.list= carries it, so the screen can build the
-   group tree. No operation sums a group, and there is no read of the
-   counterparties under a parent counterparty: a client assembles the tree from
-   the full list. The roll-up is the screen's arithmetic, and the screen must
-   state that the group figure and its members' figures come from the same rows,
-   so a reader can check one against the other.
-6. *The booking that gave the netting set is versioned, and the run names no
-   version.* A re-papering into another netting set cuts a new version of the
-   trade's booking, and the run carries no booking version and no as-of time, so
-   the screen reads the booking current when it draws and can disagree with the
-   netting set the engine actually used.
-7. *A trade with no counterparty is legal, and nothing reports the size of the
-   gap.* =ores_trading_trades_tbl= allows =counterparty_id= to be null when
-   =counterparty_scope= is =intra_entity=, so a run can hold a trade that no
-   counterparty claims. The screen draws it as a stated case, and the run's own
-   total is the only figure that says how much of the run sits outside every
-   counterparty.
-8. *The error permissions sit too high.* =reporting::report_error_events:read= is
-   held by no role below =TenantAdmin= and =SuperAdmin=. A credit reader who can
-   open the counterparty view and its trades cannot read the errors that say what
-   is missing from their figures, which is the one warning this screen exists to
-   carry alongside the number.

-#+title: User Journey: See the reports a party runs
-#+description: A person opens reporting and reads every report definition their party owns, with the health of each one's latest run, and can tell a clean run from one carrying errors without opening it.
-#+type: user_journey
-#+level: cross
-#+filetags: :knowledge:user_journey:reporting:
-#+created: 2026-10-17
-#+updated: 2026-10-17
-#+startup: inlineimages
-
-This page documents a [[id:F44766FA-1E9C-416F-849A-E131101B2ECA][user journey]]: A person opens reporting and reads every report definition their party owns, with the health of each one's latest run, and can tell a clean run from one carrying errors without opening it.
-
-A user journey describes what one person is trying to do, before anything is
-built. It is a design document that outlives any sprint, so it names the
-screens, the entity fields each screen shows, and the operations and messages
-each step needs.
-
-* Goal
-
-"Which reports does my party run, and how did each one last go?" The person
-opens one screen and gets one row per report definition their party owns. Each
-row answers four questions: what the report is called, when it runs, how its
-latest run ended, and, when that run carries errors, how many. The journey is
-done when every row has a health word the person can act on, including the row
-of a report that has never run at all.
-
-The question is the front door of the group. A person arrives without an
-identifier, so the screen must answer it from the party alone. Every other
-journey in this group starts from a row this screen draws.
-
-* Actor and trigger
-
-Three actors read the same screen: the trading desk, the market risk function
-and the tenant administrator. They read the same activity over different
-visible sets, and the sets are the permissions and the row-level policy, not
-three screens. A trading desk reads the definitions of the party it works in, a
-market risk reader reads the same rows for sign-off, and a tenant administrator
-reads every party of their tenant because the administrator holds the tenant's
-permissions in full. For a party user the session supplies the party and every
-row is party-scoped by row-level security; a tenant administrator's rows span
-the tenant's parties, so the table adds a party column and the filter can narrow
-to one.
-
-The trigger is a routine question with a deadline. A trading desk opens it at
-the start of the day, before the first number is quoted. A market risk reader
-opens it for sign-off, after the overnight runs should have finished. A tenant
-administrator opens it when a person reports that a report did not run, or when
-the same report fails twice. The journey begins when the person opens the
-reporting area and ends when they have read the health of every row they came
-for.
-
-This is a read-only monitoring journey. It creates nothing, changes nothing and
-destroys nothing. It reads the definitions, the runs, the runs' errors and the
-error scopes, and it subscribes to the run events so a row that finishes while
-the screen is open updates itself.
-
-* Steps
-
-1. *Open the reporting area.* The person opens reporting. The system shows one
-   screen: a header that names the party, a summary that counts the definitions
-   by health, and a table with one row per definition the party owns. The
-   header states the party code, for example ACMCOR, so a reader who works in
-   more than one party knows which one they are reading; a tenant
-   administrator's header names the tenant, and the rows carry their party. A
-   party that owns no definition is stated as such, not shown as an empty table
-   with no explanation.
-2. *Read the rows.* Each row states the definition's name, its report type, the
-   schedule expression it carries, when its latest run started, and its health.
-   Every seeded definition is of type =risk=, and one type is registered: =risk=,
-   the full ORE risk analytics run. The names are the seed's thirty-one: Group
-   Consolidated Exposure, Large Exposures, Liquidity Coverage, Headline Position,
-   SA-CCR Exposure, Intraday Risk Monitor and the rest. A definition with a
-   schedule expression is *scheduled*; one the party runs by hand is
-   *on-demand*. The row states which, because the two answer different
-   expectations: a scheduled report that has not run by now is late, and an
-   on-demand report that has not run is waiting for a person.
-3. *Read the health of the latest run.* The health column is one of five words.
-   The screen derives it from the definition's latest run, never from the
-   definition's own state, because a definition can be perfectly healthy while
-   its last run failed.
-   - *Never run*: the definition has no run. The row says so, and it does not
-     read as clean, because nothing ran and nothing was checked.
-   - *Running*: a run exists, it has started, and it has not completed. The row
-     prefers *running* over any earlier attempt's result: a person asking how
-     the report last went means the run in flight, not the last one that
-     finished.
-   - *Completed clean*: the latest run completed and recorded no error.
-   - *Completed while carrying errors*: the latest run completed and recorded at
-     least one error. This is normal and expected: the engine finished, wrote
-     its report, and said in its own log that a trade would not build. The
-     report still succeeded, and the health word says so rather than turning
-     the row red as a failure.
-   - *Failed*: the latest run failed and has no output to read.
-4. *Tell a run carrying errors from a clean one without opening it.* The health
-   word alone is not enough: *completed while carrying errors* is long, and two
-   completed rows must separate at a glance. The errors cell therefore carries
-   the count and the worst severity, for example *20 errors*, and the row is
-   drawn in the warning tone while a clean completed row is drawn in the normal
-   tone. Severities are =error= and =warning=, and a run can carry both. The
-   count comes from the run's error rows, and the row states it without the
-   person opening the run.
-5. *Compare the latest runs.* A completed row states when the run started and
-   when it completed, so a reader can see that the overnight run took longer
-   than yesterday's, or that the run the desk asked for at 08:10 has already
-   finished. A failed row states when it failed. A *never run* row states
-   nothing in the time columns, and that absence is the answer: the report has
-   not run, so there is no time to show.
-6. *Order the list by the question.* The list orders by name by default, which
-   is how a person looks a known report up. The health filter puts the rows a
-   reader came for at the top: *Failed*, then *Completed while carrying errors*,
-   then *Running*, then *Never run*, then *Completed clean*. A reader who asks
-   "what is broken" reads four rows instead of forty, and a reader who asks
-   "what is clean" reads the same list the other way round.
-7. *Watch the screen while runs finish.* Runs are happening while the person
-   reads. The screen subscribes to the run events, =created= and =updated=, so a
-   run that starts or finishes changes its row's health and times in place. The
-   person does not refresh to see the overnight run land. A row whose definition
-   is unknown to the subscription is not silently dropped; the screen reads the
-   definitions it owns and applies the events to the rows it holds.
-8. *A row that finished while carrying errors.* The person opens the run to read
-   why. The health word is a door, not a verdict: the row carries the run's
-   errors, and the error screen gives the scope, the subject and the engine's
-   message. That is [[id:F58B0FB5-3FD8-4BEB-982E-E54D284C0539][Find out why a run
-   went wrong]], and it is the journey a row with errors leads to.
-9. *Leave, or go on.* The person runs a report, reads what a run produced, or
-   changes when one runs next. The three writing and reading journeys are the
-   rows' own actions: [[id:76431668-8656-4276-9F9B-F292FE45B2CA][Run a report and
-   watch it finish]], [[id:969C14D2-4280-4D7C-8F51-1D395B521C83][Read what a run
-   produced]] and [[id:933649DD-1F86-4B40-99FD-1D4316D39A46][Choose when a
-   report runs]]. A person with no permission to write sees the read-only rows
-   and no action that would be refused after they press it.
-
-* Screens and wireframes
-
-One screen. The party header, the summary counts, the health filter and the
-definition table are panels of that screen, because the person reads them as one
-answer. The screen is read-only: it creates nothing, changes nothing and
-destroys nothing. The table is the whole answer, and a row carries its health
-word, its error count and its times so that no row needs opening to be
-understood.
-
-#+caption: See the reports a party runs: every definition the party owns, the health of its latest run, and a run carrying errors marked apart from a clean one.

-* Prototype
-
-The [[file:../../prototypes/reporting/see-the-reports-a-party-runs/][prototype]] argues this journey in three interpretations, and [[file:../../prototypes/reporting/see-the-reports-a-party-runs.org][its design note]] says what each argues and what is fake. This journey is the design intent for the reporting front door, and
-its prototype belongs at =doc/prototypes/reporting/see-the-reports-a-party-runs/=.
-The prototype must draw five states, one per health word, in one table so the
-five can be compared side by side: a definition that has never run, one whose
-run is in flight, one completed with no errors, one completed carrying errors
-with the count and the warning tone, and one failed. It must also draw the
-empty party, the health filter with the rows ordered by health, and a row that
-changes from *running* to *completed while carrying errors* while the page is
-open.
-
-* Entities composed
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Entity | What it contributes | Model |
-|--------+---------------------+-------|
-| =report_definition= | The row: name, report type, schedule expression, scheduler job, and the run configuration the definition carries | [[id:FB4A11C5-07EA-4923-B8AC-65F46EBA517C][ores.reporting.report_definition]] |
-| =report_instance= | The latest run of the definition: state, =output_message=, =output_storage_key=, =started_at= and =completed_at= | [[id:9FCCF6C8-9C10-403B-BDA4-C3E28706BD67][ores.reporting.report_instance]] |
-| =report_error_event= | The errors the latest run recorded: severity, scope, message and subject | [[id:080B3871-8BAA-4AAA-A98F-3E79F4B83BAA][ores.reporting.report_error_event]] |
-| =report_error_scope= | The scope vocabulary that names what an error is about | [[id:FF774B04-12E6-4BDF-B94C-222095651C4F][ores.reporting.report_error_scope]] |
-| =report_instance_kind= | The kind of run the latest run is, so a person knows it is a full run rather than one that stopped early | [[id:79A42255-AACC-43BA-B876-60D421F6DBD0][ores.reporting.report_instance_kind]] |
-| =party= | The owner of every row: the party code and name in the header, and the party each definition and run carries | [[id:8F3A1C2D-4B5E-4A6C-8F9D-2E3F4A5B6C7D][ores.refdata.party]] |
-
-The definition is the row and the run is the health. The latest run is the run
-with the greatest =started_at= among the runs whose =definition_id= is the
-definition's id; a definition with no such run is *never run*. The error count
-is the number of =report_error_event= rows whose =report_instance_id= is that
-run's id. Neither is a stored field: the screen derives both, and *What is
-missing* states the read that would spare it the join.
-
-=party_id= is on every one of these entities and every read is party-scoped by
-row-level security. The screen does not filter by party in the browser: the
-policy serves the rows, a party user sees their own party, and a tenant
-administrator sees the tenant's parties named in the party column. The
-definition and the run are
-bitemporal, so a definition edited today still states the name the earlier run
-carried; the row shows the current definition and the run's own name, and the
-two can differ.
-
-* Operations and messages
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Step | Operation | Subject | Status |
-|------+-----------+---------+--------|
-| Open the screen | List the report definitions of the party | =reporting.v1.report_definitions.list= | exists |
-| Open the screen | Read one definition | =reporting.v1.report_definitions.get= | exists |
-| Read the health | List the runs of the party | =reporting.v1.report_instances.list= | exists |
-| Read the health | Read one run | =reporting.v1.report_instances.get= | exists |
-| Read the health | Read many runs at once by their ids | =reporting.v1.report_instances.get_many= | exists |
-| Read the error count | List the errors of a run | =reporting.v1.report_error_events.list_by_report_instance_id= | exists |
-| Read the error count | Read one error | =reporting.v1.report_error_events.get= | exists |
-| Read the error count | Read the scope vocabulary | =reporting.v1.report_error_scopes.list= | exists |
-| Read the run's kind | Read the kinds a run can carry | =reporting.v1.report_instance_kinds.list= | exists |
-| Watch the screen | Learn that a run was created | =reporting.v1.report_instances_events.created= | exists |
-| Watch the screen | Learn that a run changed | =reporting.v1.report_instances_events.updated= | exists |
-| Read the schedule firing | Learn when a schedule last fired | (no read of =report_trigger_event= over NATS) | missing |
-| The screen itself | Read the definitions and their latest runs in one answer | (no BFF route) | missing |
-
-The reads are the reporting service's generated operations, and each is gated
-by a permission. The definition read checks
-=reporting::report_definitions:read=, the run read checks
-=reporting::report_instances:read=, and the error read checks
-=reporting::report_error_events:read=. The error reads are held by no role
-below =TenantAdmin= and =SuperAdmin=, so a trading desk that can see a row
-carrying errors cannot read the errors behind it until a role below those two is
-granted the read. That is a permission gap, not a screen design.
-
-The run events are the canonical change events for =report_instance=, and they
-carry the subject and the key. The screen uses them to refresh a row; it does
-not poll. No event exists for =report_error_event=, so a run that gains errors
-without changing state is caught by the run's own update or by the next read.
-
-No BFF route serves this screen. The prototype adds one, for example
-=GET /api/reporting/reports=, which reads the definitions, the latest run of
-each and the error counts, and returns the five health words already derived.
-The handler authenticates the caller's token and checks the read codes above,
-and the row-level policy narrows every read to the session's party.
-
-* What is missing
-
-1. *A route and a screen.* No BFF route serves reporting, and nothing in the web
-   application shows a report today. The screen, its summary and its health
-   filter are all new.
-2. *No read returns a definition with its latest run.* The definitions and the
-   runs are two lists, and the latest run of each definition is a join the
-   screen performs. A read of definitions with their latest run, and the count
-   of that run's errors, would make the front door one answer instead of three.
-3. *No read counts errors for a set of runs.* The screen reads one run's errors
-   at a time. A definition list of forty rows is forty error reads after the
-   run list, and a run carrying twenty errors is twenty rows. A count per run,
-   or a grouped count by scope, is the missing read.
-4. *The schedule's firing is stored and unreadable.* =report_trigger_event=
-   records a firing with its trigger type, its scheduler job and its time, and
-   there is no read of it over NATS. The screen can say a definition is
-   scheduled, and it cannot say when the schedule last fired or whether it fired
-   at all. A read of the trigger events would close that, and *What is missing*
-   on [[id:933649DD-1F86-4B40-99FD-1D4316D39A46][Choose when a report runs]]
-   states the same gap from the scheduling end.
-5. *The error permissions sit too high.* =reporting::report_error_events:read=
-   and =reporting::report_error_scopes:read= are held by no role below
-   =TenantAdmin= and =SuperAdmin=, which hold =*=. A trading desk or a market
-   risk reader can run a report and cannot read why it failed. Either the screen
-   hides the error count from them, which defeats the point of the health words,
-   or a role below the tenant administrator is granted the read.
-6. *A run that did not execute has no health word.* The five words cover a run
-   that is in flight, one that completed, and one that failed. A run that was
-   recorded and then did not execute fits none of them, and the screen must not
-   call it *failed* when nothing failed or *clean* when nothing ran. The mapping
-   is undecided, and the definition's state machine is the authority the screen
-   needs.
-7. *The definition carries no cycle and no audience.* A definition states its
-   report type and its schedule expression. The cycle a report serves is
-   =intraday= or =eod=, and its audience is one of =trading-desk=,
-   =market-risk=, =engineer= or =release check=, and both of those live on the
-   report page. The list cannot filter by either, so a reader who wants the
-   day's =eod= reports narrows the list by hand.
-8. *The latest run is a convention, not a read.* "The latest run" is the run
-   with the greatest =started_at=, and the screen derives it. A run with no
-   =started_at=, or two runs that started in the same second, has no stored
-   tie-break. The definition's run list needs an order the screen can rely on,
-   or the read needs to state the latest run itself.

-#+title: Reporting journeys
-#+description: A party's reports: which definitions it runs and how the last run of each went, running one on demand, reading what it produced, finding out what went wrong, and choosing when it runs.
-#+type: knowledge
-#+level: cross
-#+filetags: :knowledge:user_journey:reporting:
-#+created: 2026-10-17
-#+updated: 2026-10-17
-
-A report definition belongs to one party, and the party runs it on demand or on
-a schedule. Each firing creates a report instance, one record of one run, and
-the run walks the
-[[id:4F9639E5-AA68-4D47-BB05-8FA864FF9855][report execution pipeline]]: it
-prepares the engine's input, submits it to the compute grid, waits while the
-engine runs on a worker node, retrieves the output archive, and closes. The run
-records where its archive landed and every error the engine reported. These
-journeys are a person's view of that record: the reports their party owns, the
-runs of each, what a run produced, what went wrong, and when the next one
-starts.
-
-Nine journeys cover the lifecycle. The first is the front door, the one a
-reader opens with a question and no identifier: *which reports does my party
-run, and how did each one last go?* From it a person runs a report, opens what a
-run produced, reads that result by counterparty as well as by book, follows an
-error down to the trade, analytic or curve that caused it, looks back over the
-runs of one report, and changes when the report runs next. The front door is
-what makes the others reachable, so it carries the health words the whole group
-uses.
-
-Four of the nine write. Running a report creates a run, and choosing when
-it runs changes the definition's schedule. The other five read rows that a run
-already wrote. That split is why the group is cheap to build: the reporting
-service already stores the definitions, the runs, the output location and the
-errors, and every journey below reads them, with the gaps recorded in each
-journey's *What is missing*.
-
-* Journeys
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Journey | Actor | Gist |
-|---------+-------+------|
-| [[id:891DE3CB-2374-4FD9-B7FB-D8892F5174A1][See the reports a party runs]] | trading-desk, market-risk, tenant administrator | Every definition the party owns, with the latest run's health: never run, running, completed clean, completed carrying errors, or failed |
-| [[id:76431668-8656-4276-9F9B-F292FE45B2CA][Run a report and watch it finish]] | trading-desk, market-risk | Trigger one report on demand, then follow the run through its phases to a terminal state |
-| [[id:969C14D2-4280-4D7C-8F51-1D395B521C83][Read what a run produced]] | trading-desk, market-risk | The run's output message and archive, the engine's output down to one trade's result and rolled up as a book tree from a portfolio to a book to a trade, and the ORE package the run exported |
-| [[id:F58B0FB5-3FD8-4BEB-982E-E54D284C0539][Find out why a run went wrong]] | engineer, market-risk, tenant administrator | The run's errors, placed by scope and subject, down to which trade, which analytic and which curve |
-| [[id:933649DD-1F86-4B40-99FD-1D4316D39A46][Choose when a report runs]] | tenant administrator | Set the schedule that makes a definition run, run it now, pause and resume the schedule, and take it away again |
-| [[id:D6F9CB58-2A30-4124-AC05-75218272F219][See a report's results by counterparty]] | market-risk, credit, trading-desk | One run read by counterparty: each name's aggregate NPV, notional, trade count and, where the report runs =saccr=, exposure, largest first, grouped through the parent counterparty, down to one name's trades, netting sets and errors |
-| [[id:465ca244-c488-4c69-aca3-c694d104a42a][Look back over a report's history]] | trading-desk, market-risk, engineer | Every run of one report newest first, with the last five fire times, the newest marked latest, and a notice when the run being read stops being the newest |
-| [[id:7FBF8F6F-AF26-4E73-85DE-8AF72C7ED0D6][Create a report]] | tenant administrator, market-risk | Define a report: name it, bind the five configurations it reads, choose the analytics and their settings, scope it to a portfolio, and save it |
-| [[id:87B9678E-2085-4968-8AEA-7184D1384F1D][Change what a report runs]] | market-risk, tenant administrator | Turn an analytic on or off, change a parameter, and see what the change reaches: the next run of every definition sharing the configuration, and the runs it makes incomparable |
-
-* What a report is here
-
-A report is one of the report types the installation registers: =risk= and
-=grid=. Every definition the seed creates is of type =risk=, and the names a
-reader meets are the thirty-one the seed writes. They include Group Consolidated
-Exposure, Cross-Entity Counterparty Concentration, Intercompany Exposure Matrix,
-Large Exposures, Leverage Ratio, Liquidity Coverage, Board Risk Dashboard, Data
-Quality Completeness, System Health, Audit Trail Summary, Headline Position,
-SA-CCR Exposure, Intraday Risk Monitor, FRTB SA Capital, Stressed VaR,
-CVA/DVA/FVA, Bucketed DV01, Delta and Gamma, NPV, Exposure, Cashflows, Yield
-Curves, Volatility Surfaces and Credit Curves. A report page states the cycle a
-report serves, =intraday= or =eod=, and its frequency, =on-demand= or
-=scheduled=. Its audience is one of =trading-desk=, =market-risk=, =engineer= or
-=release check=. The definition row carries the report type and the schedule
-expression, which is what a screen can list; the cycle and the audience live on
-the report page.
-
-The analytics a report runs are not free choice either. A report configuration
-names a set of them, and the set is what the report's numbers come from: Headline
-Position runs =npv= and =sensitivity=, Board Risk Dashboard runs =npv=,
-=parametricVar= and =saccr=, Large Exposures runs =npv= and =saccr=, and
-Cashflows runs =cashflow=. A screen that shows a report's figures is showing
-those analytics' output and should name them.
-
-The names are not shared between parties. A definition is owned by one party,
-and the parties of a group run different reports; a reader at ACMCOR and a
-reader at ACCOUK see different definition rows even when both reports are risk
-reports. The party codes a reader meets are ACMCOR, ACCOUK, ACCOUS and ACCOHK,
-and every row below is party-scoped by row-level security rather than by a
-filter the screen applies.
-
-A *definition* is configuration and a *run* is state. The definition carries
-the name, the party, the report type, the schedule expression and the run
-configuration that decides how much of the pipeline a run executes. The run
-carries what happened: when it started, when it completed, its state, its output
-message, where its output archive landed, and its errors. A change to the
-definition affects the next run and no earlier one.
-
-* The pipeline, in the words the screens need
-
-Six phases run in order: Pre-processing, Submission, Execution, Retrieval,
-Post-processing and Finalisation. Pre-processing is four workflow steps rather
-than one, and retrieval and post-processing are one step rather than two, so the
-workflow has seven steps while the pipeline has six phases. Execution runs on a
-worker node and is not a step any ORE Studio service performs: the services
-submit the work and wait. Only finalisation touches the state machine. No phase
-calls another; the workflow engine invokes each step, and each step is handed
-the identifier or location of what the previous step produced.
-
-The seven steps are =reporting.v1.ops.gather_trades=,
-=reporting.v1.ops.gather_market_data=, =reporting.v1.ops.assemble_bundle=,
-=ore.v1.ops.prepare_ore_package=, =compute.v1.ops.submit_compute=,
-=reporting.v1.ops.collect_compute_results= and
-=reporting.v1.ops.finalise_report=. A definition whose run configuration
-substitutes pre-processing starts at =resolve_prepared_input= instead of the
-three gathering steps; one that ignores post-processing uses
-=ignore_compute_results=; and a run that cannot finish uses =fail_report=.
-
-* Who reaches the screens
-
-#+ATTR_HTML: :class hug-leading
-| Actor | What they read | What they change |
-|-------+----------------+------------------|
-| trading-desk | The definitions their party owns, the latest run of each, the outputs and the errors | Run a report on demand |
-| market-risk | The same rows, read for sign-off rather than for the desk's position | Run a report on demand |
-| engineer | The rows plus the errors, to place a failure in the engine | Nothing |
-| tenant administrator | Every row of their tenant, and the schedule of every definition | Run a report on demand; schedule a definition; pause and resume its schedule; unschedule it. Pause and resume are not available yet, because no operation sets the scheduler job's =is_active= |
-
-The reads are gated by permissions the reporting service already holds:
-=reporting::report_definitions:read=, =reporting::report_instances:read=,
-=reporting::report_error_events:read= and =reporting::report_error_scopes:read=.
-Two writes are named: =reporting::report_instances:write= and
-=reporting::report_instances:delete=. The error reads are held by no role below
-=TenantAdmin= and =SuperAdmin=, and those two hold =*=; a trading desk that can
-run a report therefore cannot read why it failed, which the group's *What is
-missing* sections state rather than paper over.
-
-* Where the screens are
-
-No BFF route serves a reporting screen, and nothing in the web application
-shows a report today. Each journey names the route it needs in *What is
-missing*, and each carries a wireframe that is the design intent for the
-prototype that will draw it. The prototypes belong under
-=doc/prototypes/reporting/=, one directory per journey, except where two journeys
-share a screen: analytic management is one prototype that both *Create a report*
-and *Change what a report runs* link to, so the interaction is written once.
-

-{
-  <b>ORE STUDIO - REPORTING: WHAT THIS REPORT RUNS</b>
-  Group Consolidated Exposure | Party ACMCOR | report type risk
-  --
-  <b>THE WIZARD: THREE STEPS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Step | What the step carries
-    1 | the definition and the configurations it binds
-    2 | the analytics, as the switchboard
-    3 | review and save
-  }
-  [ Back ] | [ Next: the analytics ]
-  --
-  <b>STEP 1 - THE DEFINITION AND THE CONFIGURATIONS IT BINDS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Configuration type | What it supplies | Where that data lives
-    conventions | calendars, day counts, pairs | /refdata/conventions -> Conventions
-    pricing_engines | engine per product family | NO SCREEN, no route exists
-    todays_market | curves, surfaces, FX spots | NO SCREEN, no route exists
-    curve_configuration | builder and pillars per curve | NO SCREEN, no route exists
-    risk_report_config | the analytics and their settings | NO SCREEN, no route exists
-  }
-  Only conventions has a screen today: PATHS.conventions, /refdata/conventions.
-  The other four are stated as missing, never drawn as links that would not resolve.
-  Group risk configuration carries the analytics, and four definitions bind it:
-  this one, Board Risk Dashboard, Group DV01 by book, Treasury Sensitivity.
-  Everything steps 2 and 3 change reaches all four.
-  --
-  <b>STEP 2 - THE ANALYTICS OF THE BOUND CONFIGURATION</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    on | display_order | analytic
-    3  | 1 | npv
-    3  | 5 | simulation
-    1  | 6 | pfe
-  }
-  The step reads the set and states the ownership: the rows hang off the run
-  settings configuration the previous step bound, so every definition bound to
-  it runs the same set. Two ways out are offered, and neither writes here:
-  --
-  <b>SET THE ANALYTICS - A SHARED SCREEN</b>
-  --
-  The switchboard, one step per analytic that is on, the parameters and the
-  rule between analytics belong to their own prototype,
-  doc/prototypes/reporting/manage-the-analytics/, which this journey links to.
-  Both this journey and Create a report use it, so the interaction is drawn
-  once rather than twice.
-  --
-  <b>THE RULE BETWEEN ANALYTICS, SHOWN AS A STATE</b>
-  --
-  <b>THIS SET CANNOT RUN: pfe is on and simulation is off.</b> The shared screen
-  marks both rows and refuses the pair. The rule lives in the ACME seeder at
-  check_exposure_needs_simulation, and no service validates it, so the screen
-  holds the refusal that the platform does not.
-  --
-  <b>DEFERRED:</b> simulation and pfe need purpose-built editors for the cube, the
-  shift and the time grid. They are drawn as plain fields here, and the page says
-  so on the parameter. A plain field is not the design.
-  --
-  <b>THE ADD-ANALYTIC FLOW - SCREEN 3: THE EFFECT</b>
-  --
-  The next run of every definition bound to Group risk configuration produces it.
-  It writes one analytic row and one parameter row per parameter.
-  A run after the change is not comparable with one before it.
-  <b><color:red>REFUSED: pfe needs simulation, and it is off in the set on the table.</color></b>
-  {
-    [ Turn simulation on as well ] | [ Back to the settings ] | [ Cancel ]
-  }
-  --
-  <b>STEP 3 - REVIEW AND SAVE: EXACTLY WHAT WILL BE WRITTEN</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Field | Was | Will be
-    simulation.active | Y | N, row kept at display_order 5
-    pfe.active | N | Y, display_order 6
-    pfe.exposure_cube | simulation-cube-01 | unchanged
-  }
-  <b>NOT WRITABLE YET: this set cannot run.</b> Step 2 has to turn simulation on,
-  or turn pfe off, before the wizard offers the write.
-  No row is deleted and no run is started.
-  --
-  <b>WHAT THE CHANGE DOES AND DOES NOT REACH</b>
-  --
-  Past runs keep the configuration they ran with, with their outputs and errors.
-  The configuration is shared, so every definition bound to it runs the new set on
-  its next run, including the three the person did not open.
-  A run after the change is not comparable with a run before it: the two runs did
-  not produce the same measures. The results screen marks a comparison partial
-  where a side carried errors, and cannot mark this case, because nothing says
-  which configuration version a run used.
-  --
-  <b>RUNS THE CHANGE MAKES INCOMPARABLE</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Run | Started | Configuration it ran with
-    run 41c9f0a7 | 2026-10-16 06:04 | inference from start time
-    run 5b02e6d3 | 2026-10-15 06:03 | inference from start time
-  }
-  --
-  <b>WHAT THIS SCREEN CANNOT SHOW</b>
-  --
-  A screen for four of the five configuration types: none exists, only conventions
-  has a route. The purpose-built editors for the cube, the shift and the time grid:
-  deferred. Which configuration version a run used: not readable. A configuration's
-  own version history: not readable. Whether pfe without simulation is refused: it
-  is not, by any service.
-  The screen states these absences rather than drawing a validation it does not have.
-}

-@enduml

-@startuml

-salt
-{
-  <b>ORE STUDIO - REPORTING: SCHEDULE</b>
-  --
-  <b>DEFINITION: Group Consolidated Exposure - ACMCOR</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Type | Party | Latest run
-    risk | ACMCOR | completed clean at 06:04:31
-  }
-  --
-  <b>CURRENT SCHEDULE: ON DEMAND</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    State | Schedule expression | Scheduler job
-    on demand | - | none
-  }
-  {
-    [ Set a schedule ]
-  }
-  --
-  <b>SET A SCHEDULE</b>
-  --
-  {
-    Expression [ 0 6 ~* ~* 1-5 ] | [ Schedule ]
-  }
-  Confirm: give Group Consolidated Exposure (ACMCOR) the schedule 0 6 ~* ~* 1-5?
-  {
-    [ Cancel ] | [ Schedule ]
-  }
-  --
-  <b>AFTER THE WRITE: SCHEDULED</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    State | Schedule expression | Scheduler job
-    scheduled | 0 6 ~* ~* 1-5 | a job id from scheduler_job_id
-  }
-  {
-    [ Change the expression ] | [ Run now ] | [ Pause ] | [ Unschedule ]
-  }
-  The panel states that the definition is scheduled because scheduler_job_id is
-  set. The next firing creates a run, and the run appears on the front door.
-  --
-  <b>CHANGE THE EXPRESSION</b>
-  --
-  {
-    Expression [ 0 7 ~* ~* 1-5 ] | [ Schedule ]
-  }
-  The same operation is sent with the new expression. The service reconciles the
-  definition's schedule; the screen reads the definition back and states the
-  result.
-  --
-  <b>RUN NOW, PAUSE, PLAY</b>
-  --
-  {
-    Run now | Pause | Play
-  }
-  Run now starts one run at once and leaves the schedule alone. Pause keeps the
-  expression and the job and stops them firing; Play starts them again. Neither
-  pause nor play has an operation today: the scheduler job's is_active is where
-  that state would live, so the panel draws a paused row as a fixture.
-  --
-  <b>AFTER THE WRITE: PAUSED</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    State | Schedule expression | Scheduler job | Next fire
-    paused | 0 6 ~* ~* 1-5 | kept | will not fire while paused
-  }
-  The expression and the job survive, so Play resumes the same recurrence. The
-  next fire time is unknown while paused, and the panel states no date.
-  --
-  <b>UNSCHEDULE</b>
-  --
-  {
-    Take the schedule away from Group Consolidated Exposure (ACMCOR)?
-  }
-  {
-    [ Cancel ] | [ Unschedule ]
-  }
-  Unscheduling is not pausing. It removes the expression and the job with it, so
-  there is no recurrence left to resume.
-  --
-  <b>AFTER THE WRITE: ON DEMAND AGAIN</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    State | Schedule expression | Scheduler job | Past runs
-    on demand | 0 7 ~* ~* 1-5 | none | kept
-  }
-  The definition stays and can still be run now. The runs already produced keep
-  their outputs and their errors. Unscheduling does not stop a run in flight, and
-  there is no operation here that cancels one.
-  --
-  <b>WHAT THIS PANEL CANNOT SHOW</b>
-  --
-  Last fired: not readable. Next due: not readable. The firing is a
-  report_trigger_event and no read of it exists; the scheduler job's state is
-  not read either. The schedule expression carries no time zone, so the panel
-  cannot say whose clock reads it. The screen states these absences rather than
-  inventing a next-run time.
-}
-
-@enduml

-{
-  <b>ORE STUDIO - REPORTING: CREATE A REPORT</b>
-  --
-  New definition | Party ACMCOR | Tenant administrator
-  --
-  <b>THE RAIL: COMPUTED FROM WHAT THE REPORT RUNS</b>
-  {#
-    Step | Entry | State
-    Y  | What it is | done
-    Y  | The conventions it binds | done
-    Y  | The pricing engines it binds | done
-    Y  | The market data it binds | done
-    Y  | The curve configuration it binds | done
-    Y  | The run settings it binds | done
-    7  | What it runs: the switchboard | current
-    | <b>the analytic steps: one per analytic that is on, in display_order</b> |
-    8  | Net present value | ahead
-    9  | Simulation | ahead
-    10 | Potential future exposure | ahead
-    | <b>the final step</b> |
-    11 | Review and save | ahead, final
-  }
-  Seven fixed steps, then one step for every analytic that is on, then the final
-  review. The rail is one list, so the rail, the step numbering and the step foot
-  agree at every moment: turning an analytic on adds its entry and renumbers the
-  ones after it, and turning one off removes it and renumbers them again.
-  --
-  <b>THE RAIL AT LENGTH</b>
-  --
-  Fifteen or more entries is a normal length, so the column sticks to the top of
-  the page and scrolls inside itself, the entries are denser, an analytic entry
-  carries its code, a divider opens the analytic run and another opens the
-  review, and a caption states the shape: "11 steps: 7 fixed, 3 analytics in
-  display order, and the final review". The current entry is scrolled into view
-  after every render. The grammar does not change: the same two-column grid, the
-  same done, current and ahead marks, the same step foot.
-  --
-  <b>DEEP LINKS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Link | Resolves to
-    ?step=7 | position 7 of the current rail
-    ?step=9&analytic=simulation | the same entry, named as well as numbered
-    ?analytic=pfe | that analytic's step, whatever its number
-  }
-  The number moves when an analytic before it is turned on or off; the code does
-  not. Navigation writes both into the URL, so a reload lands on the same step.
-  An analytic the configuration does not carry resolves to What it runs with its
-  row marked and the reason stated, never to a step that does not exist.
-  --
-  <b>STEP 1 - WHAT IT IS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Field | Value
-    Name | Intraday Exposure
-    Description | Exposure profiles
-    Report type | risk
-    Is official | yes
-    Concurrency policy | skip
-  }
-  The report type is a combo box over ores_reporting_report_types_tbl. risk is
-  the one type registered today and it names report_execution_workflow. More
-  types are expected, so the control reads the table rather than a fixed pair.
-  The party comes from the session and is not a choice.
-  --
-  <b>STEPS 2 TO 6 - ONE STEP FOR EACH CONFIGURATION TYPE</b>
-  --
-  Five steps, in the order report_type_configuration_types states and the seeder
-  writes: conventions, pricing_engines, todays_market, curve_configuration,
-  risk_report_config. Every one carries the same four parts, so two steps can be
-  read side by side: what binding that configuration means, where its data
-  lives, the picker, and what the binding reaches and what it does not.
-  --
-  <b>STEP 2 - THE CONVENTIONS IT BINDS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Part | What the step says
-    Means | The market terms every trade in the run is read with
-    Data | ores.refdata.bond_yield_convention.org, and 24 more
-    Screen | PATHS.conventions = /refdata/conventions
-    Reaches | Every instrument family, its day count and its calendars
-    Not | It creates no convention and names no market data
-  }
-  {
-    [ Group conventions ]
-  }
-  Binding it decides what a trade means. The same trade read under two convention
-  sets gives two different numbers, and neither of them is a mistake.
-  --
-  <b>STEP 3 - THE PRICING ENGINES IT BINDS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Part | What the step says
-    Means | The model and the engine each product is priced with
-    Data | pricing_model_config, pricing_model_product, its parameters
-    Screen | no screen holds a pricing engine configuration
-    Reaches | Every analytic that prices a trade, npv first
-    Not | It names no market data and builds no curve
-  }
-  {
-    [ Group pricing engines ]
-  }
-  Binding it decides how a trade is priced. A product the configuration carries no
-  row for has no model in this run.
-  --
-  <b>STEP 4 - THE MARKET DATA IT BINDS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Part | What the step says
-    Means | The data a run prices against, by market role
-    Data | todays_market_collection, configuration and its bindings
-    Screen | no screen holds a today's market configuration
-    Reaches | Every price, and the quotes each curve is built from
-    Not | It holds references by name, and fixes no valuation date
-  }
-  {
-    [ Group today's market ]
-  }
-  Binding it decides which configuration block each market role reads, and the
-  role binding is written with configuration_market_bindings.put.
-  --
-  <b>STEP 5 - THE CURVE CONFIGURATION IT BINDS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Part | What the step says
-    Means | The recipes a run builds its curves from
-    Data | curve_configuration and curve_configuration_section
-    Screen | no screen holds a curve configuration
-    Reaches | Every analytic that discounts, projects or reads a volatility
-    Not | It holds no quote, and it builds nothing
-  }
-  {
-    [ Group curve configuration ]
-  }
-  Binding it decides which recipes the run has. Without the recipe the curve is
-  not built, whatever the market quotes.
-  --
-  <b>STEP 6 - THE RUN SETTINGS IT BINDS</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Part | What the step says
-    Means | Base currency, observation model, threading, VaR and SIMM settings
-    Data | risk_report_config, and its portfolio and book junction tables
-    Screen | no screen holds a risk report configuration
-    Reaches | Run behaviour, the analytics, and the portfolio and book scope
-    Not | It carries no market data, no curve and no model
-  }
-  {
-    [ Exposure simulation - Group Treasury Portfolio ]
-  }
-  The scope lives here and not on the definition, which is why the definition
-  chooses no portfolio. No operation in this journey's set writes the settings or
-  the scope: both come from the seeder.
-  --
-  <b>STEP 7 - WHAT IT RUNS: THE SWITCHBOARD, AND THE INDEX OF THE STEPS AFTER IT</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    On | Analytic | Order | Step | One-line summary
-    Y | npv | 1 | 8 | one present value per trade, netted to book
-    Y | simulation | 2 | 9 | simulated paths, and the cube pfe reads
-    Y | pfe | 3 | 10 | an exposure profile per counterparty and date
-    N | saccr | 4 | -- | the row is kept at display_order 4
-  }
-  Fourteen analytic types, one row each: the switch, the display order and a
-  one-line summary of what the analytic produces. This step is the index, not a
-  place to edit settings. A row that is on states the number of the step it owns
-  and carries a control that goes straight to it.
-  --
-  <b>TURNING ONE ON, AND TURNING ONE OFF</b>
-  --
-  The switch is how an analytic is added. Turning a type on writes its
-  configuration_analytic row with the default value of every parameter and gives
-  it a step in display_order. Turning one off asks first, because the settings
-  leave the rail with the step, and because the write is active false and not a
-  deletion: the row keeps its display_order and its parameter rows, so a later
-  reader can see the report used to produce it. Nothing on the page deletes a
-  row.
-  {
-    [ Turn simulation off?  Its 3 parameter values go with the step. The row is
-      set to active = false and is not deleted.  ( Turn simulation off ) ( Keep it on ) ]
-  }
-  --
-  <b>ANALYTIC STEP 8 - NET PRESENT VALUE, ONE OF THREE SUCH STEPS</b>
-  --
-  What net present value is: what the book is worth today, priced against today's
-  curves and added up the book tree.
-  How it is calculated: each trade's future cashflows are projected, discounted
-  at the discount curve and summed, and the sums roll up from trade to book to
-  portfolio.
-  {
-    Parameter | Control | Note
-    discount_curve | text | the curve the cashflows are discounted at
-    include_cashflows | switch | write each cashflow row as well as the total
-  }
-  Every parameter carries a control chosen for the shape of its value, a note on
-  what it means and what a normal value looks like. An analytic that takes no
-  parameter says so rather than showing an empty list.
-  <b>The settings below are rows of Exposure simulation - Group Treasury
-  Portfolio, not of this definition:</b> 6 definitions bind that configuration,
-  so a value changed here reaches their next run too.
-  {
-    [ Turn npv off ]  ...  ( Back ) ( Next: simulation )
-  }
-  --
-  <b>THE pfe AND simulation PAIR IS A STATE, NOT A BLOCKED CLICK</b>
-  --
-  Turning pfe on is allowed: its step appears, and the rule strip on step 7 marks
-  both the pfe row and the simulation row. The pfe step states that it cannot run,
-  and the save refuses the pair.
-  pfe reads the cube that simulation writes. The rule lives in the ACME seeder, in
-  generate_risk_config_data.py at check_exposure_needs_simulation, and nothing in
-  the reporting service validates it when a definition is written. The screen
-  refuses the pair itself, and a build would have to carry the rule again.
-  --
-  <b>FINAL STEP - REVIEW AND SAVE</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Written | Operation
-    definition | report_definitions.put
-    five binds | report_configurations.put
-    analytic rows | configuration_analytics.put_many
-    param rows | configuration_analytic_parameters.put
-    the scope | no operation
-  }
-  Every field value is named, including the ones that stay empty: name Intraday
-  Exposure, report_type risk, is_official true, concurrency_policy skip,
-  schedule_expression none, scheduler_job_id none, fsm_state_id none,
-  run_grant_id none, pre_processing execute, prepared_input_key null,
-  post_processing execute. Also the analytic rows with their active and
-  display_order, which are the analytic steps of the rail in that order; their
-  parameter values; and the portfolio scope the bound configuration carries.
-  {
-    [ Save the report ]
-  }
-  The read-back states the stored row with report_definitions.get, that the
-  definition is on demand, and that it has never run.
-  This step is final, so its rail entry carries the final tag and its foot
-  carries no Back. Going back is refused at the first step and at a final step.
-  --
-  <b>WHAT THIS SCREEN CANNOT SHOW</b>
-  --
-  No operation answers what a report needs in order to run beyond the
-  configuration types its report type requires. Nothing validates the
-  pfe-needs-simulation rule on write. No operation writes the portfolio scope or
-  the run settings. Four of the five configuration types have no screen. No
-  operation stages an analytic set for one definition, so the rail is a view over
-  rows already written to a shared configuration. The rail primitive cannot mark
-  an unfit step, group its entries or collapse them. No BFF route serves
-  reporting, and nothing in the application creates a report today.
-}
-
-@enduml

-{
-  <b>ORE STUDIO - REPORTING: RUN OUTPUTS</b>
-  --
-  <b>RUN: Group Consolidated Exposure - 4b7e1a02</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    State | Completed | Took | Kind
-    completed | 08:15:02 | 2 m 18 s | from report_instance_kind
-  }
-  --
-  <b>WHAT THE SYSTEM SAID</b>
-  --
-  {
-    Output message: Report execution completed.
-  }
-  --
-  <b>THE ENGINE'S OUTPUT ARCHIVE</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Archive | reporting/runs/<instance-id>/output.tar.gz | [ Download ]
-  }
-  The archive is the run's output directory, archived by the compute run. This
-  screen does not list the files inside it: no operation lists an archive's
-  contents, so the reader opens the archive. An empty file list is not drawn.
-  --
-  <b>WHAT THE RUN SAID WAS WRONG</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Severity | Scope | Count
-    error | Analytics | 8
-    warning | Configuration | 3
-  }
-  11 rows in all. The archive is complete and the run still carries these. Open
-  the errors for the subject of each one.
-  --
-  <b>ONE ROW PER TRADE</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    TradeId | TradeType | NPV | NPV(Base) | Notional | CounterParty
-    2d0f8a31-5e6c-4b79-a1d2-7c4e9f3b6a05 | Bond | - | - | 40,000,000 | ACME BANK PLC  [error]
-    2df8fa31-5dc6-4b79-a1d7-7c4e9f3b6a05 | Bond | 1,284,402.00 | 1,516,004.75 | 40,000,000 | NORTHGATE CLEARING
-  }
-  The per-trade table is =npv.csv='s own columns, one row per trade. The failed
-  trade carries no price because a trade the engine could not build writes no NPV
-  row; its row links to the error recorded against that =TradeId=. Where the
-  archive named a trade by its id, the trade is the trading trade with that id,
-  and =trading.v1.trades.get= resolves it. No operation parses the archive, so
-  this table is a fixture until a result store or an archive read exists.
-  --
-  <b>THE ORE PACKAGE THIS RUN USED</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Pre-processing | Package | Action
-    execute | prepared by ore.v1.ops.prepare_ore_package | [ Open package ]
-    substitute | prepared_input_key from the definition | [ Open package ]
-  }
-  The package is the engine's input. It is what a person would run locally to
-  reproduce the output. No read in the set returns it or lists its files.
-  --
-  <b>A RUN IN FLIGHT: NO OUTPUT YET</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    State | Started | Output message | Archive
-    running | 08:12:44 | - | not yet retrieved
-  }
-  The archive key is written only once the run's results are retrieved. The panel
-  says the output will arrive; it does not show an empty archive.
-  --
-  <b>A RUN THAT FAILED: NOTHING TO TAKE</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    State | Output message | Archive | Package
-    failed | - | none | none
-  }
-  There is no archive and no package to hand over. The screen says so and sends
-  the reader to the run's errors, including the Report scope rows the model
-  states itself when no engine saw the failure.
-}

-{
-  <b>ORE STUDIO - REPORTING: RESULTS BY COUNTERPARTY</b>
-  --
-  <b>RUN: Cross-Entity Counterparty Concentration - 4b7e1a02</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Party | Runs | State | Took
-    ACMCOR | npv, saccr | completed | 2 m 18 s
-  }
-  --
-  <b>THE COUNTERPARTIES THIS RUN IS EXPOSED TO</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Code | Counterparty | NPV USD m | Notional USD m | Trades | Exposure USD m | Share
-    . | <b>MERIDIAN CAPITAL GROUP</b> | 12.5 | 2,418.0 | 1,742 | 918.4 | 14.1%
-    MERID | Meridian Capital | 8.2 | 1,610.0 | 1,204 | 604.3 | 9.3%
-    MERID-UK | Meridian Capital UK | 4.3 | 808.0 | 538 | 314.2 | 4.8%
-    . | <b>ACME BANK PLC</b> | 21.9 | 3,902.0 | 2,318 | 1,486.3 | 24.8%
-    ACMEBK | ACME Bank PLC | 21.9 | 3,902.0 | 2,318 | 1,486.3 | 24.8%
-    NRTHCLR | NORTHGATE CLEARING | 9.1 | 1,744.0 | 906 | 512.9 | 10.3%
-    HANSAPF | HANSA PFANDBRIEF | 2.9 | 622.0 | 214 | 88.7 | 3.3%
-    PACTRST | PACIFIC TRUST | 1.7 | 418.0 | 168 | 41.2 | 1.9%
-    KSTLASR | KESTREL ASSURANCE | 0.9 | 212.0 | 96 | 18.4 | 1.0%
-    . | <b>Total, largest first</b> | 88.4 | 18,204.0 | 18,204 | 3,248.5 | 100%
-  }
-  Largest first, by exposure where the report runs =saccr= and by aggregate NPV
-  where it does not. A group row sits above its members and carries the sum of
-  them; a member keeps its own figure because the desk faces the member and
-  credit faces the group. No operation returns a result grouped by counterparty,
-  and nothing parses the archive, so every figure here is a fixture.
-  --
-  <b>ONE COUNTERPARTY: ACME BANK PLC (ACMEBK)</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Netting Set | Trades | NPV USD m | Exposure USD m | Errors
-    ACME-CSA-1 | 1,842 | 17.2 | 1,180.4 | 0
-    ACME-CSA-2 | 476 | 4.7 | 305.9 | 2
-  }
-  {#
-    Trade | Type | Notional USD m | NPV | Netting Set | Error
-    2df8fa31... | Swap | 40.0 | 1.28 | CSA-1 | -
-    2d0f8a31... | Bond | 40.0 | - | CSA-2 | Analytics
-  }
-  The trade is the trading trade with that id, and the trade names its
-  counterparty_id. The error scopes are Trade, Analytics, Curve, Configuration
-  and Report: none of them is a counterparty, so a counterparty's errors are
-  reached through the trades that name it, and an error recorded against the
-  analytic alone is not divided across names.
-  --
-  <b>A COUNTERPARTY WITH NO RESULT</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Code | Counterparty | NPV | Notional | Trades | Exposure | Share
-    BLUERIV | BLUE RIVER PENSION | - | - | 0 | - | -
-  }
-  The party can see this counterparty and the run produced nothing for it. It is
-  listed, not dropped, and it is not a measure of zero.
-  --
-  <b>A TRADE THAT NAMES NO COUNTERPARTY</b>
-  --
-  {#
-    Heading | Trades | Notional USD m | NPV USD m
-    counterparty_scope = intra_entity | 412 | 980.0 | 1.2
-  }
-  The schema allows counterparty_id to be null when the scope is intra_entity. The
-  run's counterparty totals are less than the run's total by this amount, and the
-  screen says so rather than folding it into a name.
-}
