+TEST_CASE("fx_exotic_mapper_keeps_a_range_bound_level_digits", tags) {
+    auto lg(make_logger(test_suite));
+
+    // A float carries at most nine significant digits, so a level the document
+    // states with more digits survives only if the binding keeps the text and
+    // the column stores the decimal. The document here states the level with
+    // twelve digits after the point.
+    using ores::platform::filesystem::file;
+    auto content = file::read_content(example_path("Exotic_FxAccumulator.xml"));
+    const std::string as_written = "<RangeTo>122</RangeTo>";
+    const std::string with_digits = "<RangeTo>122.123456789012</RangeTo>";
+    const auto at = content.find(as_written);
+    REQUIRE(at != std::string::npos);
+    content.replace(at, as_written.size(), with_digits);
+
+    portfolio p;
+    ores::ore::domain::load_data(content, p);
+    REQUIRE(!p.Trade.empty());
+    const auto mapped = ores::ore::domain::trade_mapper::map_fx_instrument(p.Trade.front());
+    REQUIRE(mapped.has_value());
+    REQUIRE(mapped->range_bounds.size() == 2);
+    REQUIRE(mapped->range_bounds[0].range_to.has_value());
+    CHECK(mapped->range_bounds[0].range_to->to_string() == "122.123456789012");
+
+    auto rt = fx_instrument_mapper::reverse_fx_accumulator(mapped->accumulators.front(),
+                                                           mapped->range_bounds);
+    portfolio out;
+    out.Trade.push_back(std::move(rt));
+    const auto written = ores::ore::domain::save_data(out);
+    CHECK(written.contains("<RangeTo>122.123456789012</RangeTo>"));
+}

+/**
+ * @brief Stores a conventions document.
+ *
+ * The instrument conventions belong to the session's party and replace any
+ * it holds under the same id. A world convention the tenant lacks is added;
+ * one it holds is left as it is.
+ */
+struct save_conventions_document_request {
+    using response_type = struct save_conventions_document_response;
+    static constexpr std::string_view nats_subject = "refdata.v1.conventions_documents.put";
+    /**
+     * @brief Whether the caller must have established a session first.
+     *
+     * An operation that produces the session cannot present one, so a client
+     * reads this rather than assuming every call carries a token.
+     */
+    static constexpr bool requires_session = true;
+    conventions_document document;
+};

+/**
+ * @brief What the save did not store, and why.

+struct save_conventions_document_response {

+void configuration_document_handler::save_conventions_document(ores::nats::message msg) {
+    const auto ctx = authorise(nats_, ctx_, msg, verifier_, "refdata::conventions:write");
+    if (!ctx)
+        return;
+    const auto req = decode<save_conventions_document_request>(msg);
+    if (!req) {
+        error_reply(nats_, msg, ores::service::error_code::bad_request);
+        return;
+    }
+    try {
+        require_party(*ctx);
+        const auto saved = service::conventions_document_service(*ctx).save(req->document);
+        reply(nats_,
+              msg,
+              save_conventions_document_response{
+                  .success = true, .world_kept = saved.world_kept, .fx_skipped = saved.fx_skipped});
+    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
+        BOOST_LOG_SEV(lg(), warn) << msg.subject << " refused: " << e.what();
+        reply(nats_, msg, save_conventions_document_response{.message = e.what()});
+    }
+}
+
+void configuration_document_handler::get_conventions_document(ores::nats::message msg) {
+    const auto ctx = authorise(nats_, ctx_, msg, verifier_, "refdata::conventions:read");
+    if (!ctx)
+        return;
+    const auto req = decode<get_conventions_document_request>(msg);
+    if (!req) {
+        error_reply(nats_, msg, ores::service::error_code::bad_request);
+        return;
+    }
+    try {
+        service::conventions_document_service svc(for_requested_party(*ctx, req->party_id));
+        reply(
+            nats_, msg, get_conventions_document_response{.success = true, .document = svc.get()});
+    } catch (const std::exception& e) {
+        BOOST_LOG_SEV(lg(), warn) << msg.subject << " refused: " << e.what();
+        reply(nats_, msg, get_conventions_document_response{.message = e.what()});
+    }
+}
+
 }

+    note right of ores_trading_range_bounds_tbl
+    AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
+    Template: sql_schema_domain_entity_create.mustache
+    To modify, update the template and regenerate.
+    Range Bound Table
+    One row per entry in the RangeBounds list an accumulator document
+    states, keyed to the trade and the entry's ordinal. The list holds the
+    levels an accumulator accrues against, so the entry is the unit the
+    document writes and the unit the table stores.
+    The ORE schema states the list as unbounded RangeBound entries and
+    requires at least one; each entry carries an optional start date as an
+    attribute and the optional levels RangeFrom, RangeTo, Leverage,
+    Strike and StrikeAdjustment. The order is the document's order, and
+    the ordinal preserves it, so export re-emits the entries as the document
+    held them.
+    A level is money unless it is a ratio. RangeFrom, RangeTo, Strike
+    and StrikeAdjustment are price levels, so each column is exact decimal.
+    Leverage is a multiplier, so the column is a binary double, the same
+    way a basket weight is. A document that states no level leaves the
+    column null rather than a zero it never wrote.
+    The rows are keyed by the trade alone, so any instrument whose document
+    states a RangeBounds list can own them. The FX accumulator is the first
+    to write them. The equity accumulator still carries the list as JSON text
+    and moves onto this table in its own unit.
+    end note

+    note right of ores_trading_range_bounds_tbl
+    AUTO-GENERATED FILE - DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY
+    Template: sql_schema_domain_entity_create.mustache
+    To modify, update the template and regenerate.
+    Range Bound Table
+    One row per entry in the RangeBounds list an accumulator document
+    states, keyed to the trade and the entry's ordinal. The list holds the
+    levels an accumulator accrues against, so the entry is the unit the
+    document writes and the unit the table stores.
+    The ORE schema states the list as unbounded RangeBound entries and
+    requires at least one; each entry carries an optional start date as an
+    attribute and the optional levels RangeFrom, RangeTo, Leverage,
+    Strike and StrikeAdjustment. The order is the document's order, and
+    the ordinal preserves it, so export re-emits the entries as the document
+    held them.
+    A level is money unless it is a ratio. RangeFrom, RangeTo, Strike
+    and StrikeAdjustment are price levels, so each column is exact decimal.
+    Leverage is a multiplier, so the column is a binary double, the same
+    way a basket weight is. A document that states no level leaves the
+    column null rather than a zero it never wrote.
+    The rows are keyed by the trade alone, so any instrument whose document
+    states a RangeBounds list can own them. The FX accumulator is the first
+    to write them. The equity accumulator still carries the list as JSON text
+    and moves onto this table in its own unit.
+    end note

+std::vector<domain::range_bound>
+read_range_bounds_by_trade_ids(context ctx, const std::vector<std::string>& trade_ids) {
+    if (trade_ids.empty())
+        return {};
+    static const auto max(make_timestamp(MAX_TIMESTAMP, lg()));
+    const auto tid = ctx.tenant_id().to_string();
+    const auto query =
+        sqlgen::read<std::vector<range_bound_entity>> |
+        where("tenant_id"_c == tid && "trade_id"_c.in(trade_ids) && "valid_to"_c == max.value()) |
+        order_by("trade_id"_c, "sequence_number"_c);
+
+    return execute_read_query<range_bound_entity, domain::range_bound>(
+        ctx,
+        query,
+        [](const auto& entities) { return range_bound_mapper::map(entities); },
+        lg(),
+        "Reading range bounds by instrument ids.");
+}
